Join Our Dynamic Team as a Cloud Services Engineer! 🌟

Are you passionate about telecoms? Do you thrive in a fast‑paced, innovative environment? At Babble, we’re on a mission to be our customers’ most trusted advisor for cloud‑based technologies. We’re looking for passionate and talented individuals to join our dynamic team. If so, we have the perfect opportunity for you!

What will you be doing?

The purpose of this role is to take senior, hands‑on ownership of the organisation’s cloud services environment, ensuring it is secure, reliable, cost‑effective, and continuously improving. You will be responsible for managing, developing, and maintaining services across Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, and the Cisco Meraki environment, supporting modern ways of working and delivering high‑quality internal technology services.

The Cloud Services Engineer is accountable for the stability, performance, security, and continual improvement of the core cloud and network platforms that underpin day‑to‑day operations, particularly Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, and Cisco Meraki.

The role also supports a small on‑premises domain controller environment during its transition to full cloud operation. This includes planning and executing decommissioning activities in a controlled, low‑risk manner. Working closely with internal stakeholders and suppliers, you will ensure the platform estate is well governed, appropriately automated, and operated in line with modern best practice, including backup and disaster recovery readiness.

Accountabilities and Deliverables:

The role holder will be directly accountable for delivering the following operational and improvement objectives, with measurable outcomes aligned to agreed service standards, security requirements, and operational performance measures. A hands‑on approach is required where necessary.

Infrastructure, Cloud & Corporate Platforms

  • Manage and maintain Microsoft Azure services to agreed availability, performance, and security standards, including monitoring, patching and updates (where applicable), backup and restore processes, capacity management, and lifecycle governance.
  • Act as a senior technical escalation point for cloud services incidents and problems, driving effective triage, root‑cause analysis, remediation, and preventative improvements. Develop and maintain operational runbooks and documentation to improve reliability and response.
  • Own the ongoing evolution of the cloud services estate, improving security posture, automation, resilience, and cost efficiency. Provide day‑to‑day oversight of suppliers supporting Azure, Microsoft 365, and Meraki services, monitoring service quality and escalating issues as required.
  • Maintain and support the remaining on‑premises domain controller environment during the transition period, including identity and DNS dependencies. Deliver a planned and documented decommissioning approach with appropriate testing, rollback planning, and stakeholder communication.
  • Own and maintain backup and disaster recovery services for cloud and hybrid infrastructure, including defining recovery procedures, testing restore capabilities, maintaining DR runbooks, and ensuring recovery point and recovery time objectives are documented and achievable.

Network, Connectivity & Operations

  • Manage and maintain the Cisco Meraki environment (switching, wireless, and security appliances as applicable), ensuring consistent configuration, monitoring, firmware lifecycle management, and secure network access aligned to agreed standards.
  • Ensure network and cloud service incidents are logged, tracked, and resolved within agreed response and resolution targets. Contribute to post‑incident reviews and implement corrective and preventative actions.
  • Coordinate operational oversight for network and internet connectivity suppliers, monitoring performance against agreed benchmarks and supporting service reviews, renewals, and technical change activity.
  • Ensure the internal cloud and network environment remains a credible reference implementation, supporting technical walkthroughs and knowledge sharing where appropriate, without detracting from core operational responsibilities.

Internal IT Support & End-User Services

  • Provide senior‑level support for Microsoft 365 services (including Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive), alongside identity and access management. Ensure services are securely configured, operated to agreed standards, and that end‑user impact is minimised.
  • Support onboarding and offboarding processes and endpoint provisioning via Intune and Autopilot, including policy configuration, compliance, application deployment, and device health reporting. Work with service desk colleagues and suppliers to maintain operational readiness and supportability.
  • Collaborate with internal support teams and third‑party providers to maintain a reliable, responsive end‑user service. Identify recurring issues, enhance knowledge articles and runbooks, and automate common tasks where possible.
  • Support the configuration and ongoing management of Microsoft Teams telephony services, including Teams Phone licence allocation, call plan configuration, call queues, auto‑attendants, number assignment, and voicemail. Escalate Five9 contact centre matters to the appropriate business teams as required.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

  • Provide technical leadership across the cloud services estate by defining standards, improving documentation, mentoring peers where appropriate, and driving adoption of modern operational practices such as monitoring, automation, least‑privilege access, and secure configuration baselines.
  • Maintain visibility of cloud and licensing costs across Azure and Microsoft 365, identifying and implementing optimisation opportunities to improve value for money while balancing service quality, security, and reliability.
  • Coordinate with the Security function on vulnerability remediation, patching priorities, and security incident response activities impacting cloud and infrastructure services, ensuring timely action in line with agreed security policies and controls.
  • Support software licence and entitlement management for cloud and infrastructure services (including Azure and Microsoft 365), contributing to licence tracking, compliance reporting, cost optimisation, and renewal planning as directed by the Technical Operations Manager.
  • Ensure all infrastructure and cloud service changes follow the agreed change management process, including appropriate assessment, documentation, approval, and communication prior to implementation.

What else looks good for this role:

  • Experience driving improvement and maturity within established IT estates, rather than working solely on greenfield projects.
  • Background working within lean or small‑team environments, with a proven ability to deliver results efficiently and cost‑effectively.
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust connectivity principles or cloud‑first security frameworks, supporting continuous improvement and secure operational practices.
  • A balanced approach to operational discipline and pragmatic problem‑solving, delivering efficiency and stakeholder satisfaction in line with business objectives.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft Teams telephony services (including Teams Phone, call queues, auto‑attendants, and direct routing) within a corporate environment.
  • Extensive experience in a hands‑on Cloud, Infrastructure Engineering, or IT Operations role, with proven ownership of production services, incident and problem management, and continuous improvement aligned to agreed service standards.
  • Demonstrable practical expertise in Microsoft Azure, including core services, monitoring, security controls, and governance, with experience designing, implementing, and maintaining cloud services in a controlled and supportable manner.
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft 365 administration, including Entra ID (Azure AD), Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive, alongside device management using Intune and Autopilot to support hybrid working environments.
  • Strong background in networking and connectivity, ideally including Cisco Meraki, with experience maintaining secure wired and wireless environments and working with third‑party connectivity providers.
  • Experience supporting hybrid identity and on‑premises dependencies (such as domain controllers and DNS), with the ability to plan and safely execute decommissioning or migration activities with minimal business disruption.
  • Excellent problem‑solving skills with a customer‑centric, service‑focused mindset, able to communicate clearly with both technical and non‑technical stakeholders and take full ownership through to resolution.
  • Experience with backup, recovery, and disaster recovery planning in cloud and hybrid environments, including defining, documenting, and regularly testing recovery procedures.

Why work for Babble?

  • Risk cover, including Life Cover, Critical Illness Cover, funeral benefits, and some disability benefits.
  • 22 days’ annual leave plus UK bank holidays, with increased entitlement based on length of service.
  • 5% allowance based on basic salary, which can be allocated towards medical aid.
  • UPS provided to assist with load shedding (2–4 hours of laptop power).
  • Babble‑issued laptop.
  • Annual company celebrations.
  • Home‑working policy.

The recruitment journey

We aim to fill this role quickly while ensuring we appoint the right person. The recruitment process will begin with an initial screening call. If successful, you will then progress to an interview via Microsoft Teams, with a possible follow‑up interview and competency testing depending on the role requirements.

Direct Candidates Only

Babble is a Customer Experience-led growth business. As the ultimate Trusted Advisor for cloud-based technologies, we specialize in empowering businesses with the best solutions from the world's leading providers.

jobs.description:
At System Six, we're building one of the best places to work in cloud-accounting—a place where our team members are the most important part of our business and where they consistently experience joy, flexibility, and professional growth. We are a fast-growing, modern, 100% remote organization delivering full-cycle accounting, tax, and other professional services to hundreds of clients nationwide.

We are actively seeking a Tax Manager, a joyful and driven team member who will oversee and manage tax compliance, planning, and review for a portfolio of clients while mentoring and supporting our staff. This role blends strong technical tax expertise with people-focused leadership to ensure high-quality client service, accurate deliverables, and the professional growth of the team. The Tax Manager will report directly to the Head of Tax and will collaborate closely with other team members to deliver exceptional client and team experiences.

This is a full-time, U.S.-based position offering an opportunity to manage and grow within a thriving, ambitious, and balanced organization. System Six has grown significantly over the last five years and plans to continue to do so for decades moving forward; but importantly, we grow in a measured manner that allows all teams to find healthy fulfillment and balance in their career and personal life. This is not your traditional accounting firm with miserable busy seasons. Our talented team loves System Six and we can’t wait to show you how that energy permeates throughout our organization.

So what are we looking for in an ideal candidate?

Personal Skills

  • Excellent communication skills internally across a variety of channels
  • Adaptable communication skills externally with clients who have diverse business and financial backgrounds - simple when needed; deep and sophisticated when valuable
  • Intuition for understanding clients and knowing how to solve relationship challenges
  • Resourcefulness. An independent problem solver that can also ask for help when needed
  • Humility, patience, and a deeply rooted servant leadership mentality
  • Joy. A pleasure to work with; energetic and warm. You are enthusiastic about work daily

Professional Skills

  • 5+ years of public accounting experience, with expertise in tax compliance for individuals, S Corporations, C Corporations, and Partnerships/LLCs.
  • Skilled in federal, state, and local tax compliance and reporting, including multi-state filings and specialized areas such as R&D credits, and PTET elections.
  • Experience reviewing and signing tax returns, conducting first-level reviews of staff work, and providing actionable feedback.
  • Skilled in research, responding to tax notices, and supporting tax planning initiatives.
  • Proficiency with tax and accounting software (Lacerte and QuickBooks Online preferred, Karbon is a plus).
  • CPA or EA license required.
  • Demonstrated ability to quickly adapt to new technologies and software.

What does the day to day look like for this role?

As a Tax Manager, you will work with a department of 8 other individuals serving approximately 100 clients representing around 200 returns. We expect this to grow in the coming years as we look to grow our tax department alongside our blossoming CAS business. Your primary responsibilities are to:

  • Oversee tax compliance and review for a portfolio of clients, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and adherence to regulations.
  • Serve as the primary contact for clients, addressing tax inquiries, delivering ad hoc projects, and providing high-quality solutions.
  • Conduct first reviews of tax work prepared by staff, provide constructive feedback, and support their professional development.
  • Recommend tax strategies that support client goals and explain tax outcomes clearly
  • Mentor and train team members, fostering a collaborative and supportive environment.
  • Stay current with tax laws, regulations, and client opportunities, identifying proactive planning strategies.
  • Assist in process improvement initiatives to enhance internal workflows and client service.

Importantly, here’s what’s in it for you:

  • A joyful work environment where employees and culture are paramount. We understand that we are all human and we want your success in your professional life to elevate and empower your personal life
  • Work/Life balance. Our team enjoys our work environment, as we are anything but a traditional accounting firm. No grueling hours that you see at traditional firms; we pride ourselves on calm, smooth tax seasons where our team doesn’t pull 60+ hours or anything close to that! We work hard to take care of our physical and mental health. Our diverse team includes human parents, dog parents, hikers, yogis, mountain bikers, readers, coffee/tea lovers, avid board game players, and all-around nice people
  • A 100% remote environment. We've been remote for 10+ years and are set up for you to succeed remotely while working with flexibility during daytime professional hours
  • Strong compensation. This exempt position offers a base salary range of $95,000-$115,000 and includes a bonus structure based upon portfolio performance.
  • Competitive benefits. We provide all of your work equipment, health, dental and vision insurance, 401k matching, PTO, family leave, annual in-person gatherings and many other leading benefits
  • Growth opportunities. We are a healthily growing company on a multi-decade journey of evolution. We relish promoting from within, and will support you in your efforts to grow with System Six

Excited to apply? Here’s how!

Apply online via the link and let us know our favorite color is orange.

At System Six, we truly believe in the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance and we understand the importance of family and personal commitments. While we encourage our employees to prioritize their well-being outside of work, we do not allow team members to take on additional paid accounting tasks beyond their role with us. This is a 100% remote, work from home role. You must have strong, reliable home internet connection and an environment conducive to video and phone calls.

Hi!

We are Boosta, a holding tech company that creates, develops, and invests in digital businesses with global potential. Today, we collaborate with over 800 specialists from different parts of the world, and millions of users use our products and services.

We're currently looking for an Email Marketing Manager to join Uplift, a business building a portfolio of digital products for users’ everyday needs.

The team is currently in the early stages of formation: key technical roles are already in place, with the main focus now on building the marketing function for the first product. This is an opportunity to join the business at launch and build processes from the ground up.

What will be your focus:

  • Audit existing flows (abandoned quiz / checkout, onboarding, upsell, retention, win-back) and implement changes that drive the biggest increase in purchases.
  • Maintain a backlog of hypotheses and A/B tests — from subject lines and offers to timing and flow logic — and take every test through to a clear conclusion.
  • Segment the audience by behavior, funnel stage, geography, and quiz responses, and personalize messaging based on user data.
  • Analyze the funnel (Delivered → Open → Click → Checkout → Purchase → Revenue), work with Product and Analytics to set up tracking and attribution, and regularly report on email’s contribution to business metrics.
  • Maintain domain reputation and list health: bounce, spam, and unsubscribe rates, as well as consent and compliance requirements across Tier-1 markets.
  • Write email copy; design is handled by the UX team.
  • Propose how to grow the channel further and back your recommendations with data for the CEO.

You’re a great fit if you:

  • 2+ years of commercial experience in Email / CRM / Lifecycle Marketing for subscription-based products (B2C).
  • Experience owning email channel performance end to end - from strategy to purchases, not just campaign execution.
  • A proven example of growing email-driven revenue or sales that you can break down into steps and numbers: what you changed, how you measured it, and what impact it had.
  • Hands-on experience independently setting up and launching lifecycle and trigger-based flows with measurable results.
  • Experience running A/B tests: how you formulate hypotheses, evaluate results, and decide what to scale.
  • Ability to work with core business metrics (Purchase CR, revenue per send, LTV, retention) and assess attribution and incrementality.
  • Strong understanding of email deliverability: domain reputation, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), IP/domain warming, and recovering inbox placement.
  • Hands-on experience with ESPs (Customer.io, Reteno, Braze, Klaviyo, or similar): segmentation, flows, and reporting.
  • Experience running email campaigns across international markets (Tier-1 markets) and understanding consent requirements: GDPR / ePrivacy / CAN-SPAM / CASL.
  • At least an Intermediate level of English is required.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Amplitude, Tableau, or other analytics / BI tools.

Here’s what our hiring process looks like:

  • Stage 1. Pre-screen.
  • Stage 2. Interview.
  • Stage 3. Bar-raising (if needed).
  • Stage 4. Reference check.
  • Stage 5. Job Offer.

What’s waiting for you at Uplift?

Boost your potential:

  • Build a product from the ground up and have a say in key decisions.
  • Work in an environment that gives you the freedom and space to take action.
  • Grow alongside strong A-players who share their expertise and are always ready to boost each other.
  • Keep learning through internal and external talks, courses.

Choose your own rhythm:

  • Work remotely or from our office in Kyiv or coworking spaces in Lviv and Warsaw.
  • Plan your workday your way — we offer a flexible schedule because results matter most.
  • Take time to recharge: 28 working days of annual vacation, up to 30 days of sick leave, plus all public holidays.
  • Need more flexibility? You can move a working day to a weekend and vice versa when needed.

Keep your balance:

  • Take care of your health with medical insurance, our Mental Health program, and compensation for psychological support sessions.
  • Get involved in socially impactful initiatives, including our Ukrainian Victory Support program.
  • Celebrate important moments — receive gifts for meaningful milestones in your personal and professional life.
  • Join quarterly team-building activities, both online and offline — because strong teams are built beyond work, too.

Ready to build from scratch? Make your ambition happen here.

jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Software development is changing fast, and code is no longer written by humans alone.
jobs.description:
Software development is changing fast, and code is no longer written by humans alone. Secure Code Warrior is the AI Software Governance platform that gives organizations visibility into how their software is created, strengthens developer capability, and reduces risk before code reaches production. Built on a decade as the world's leading secure coding training platform, we're trusted by enterprises worldwide. We're a venture-backed company with offices in Australia, the United States, Belgium, Iceland, and the United Kingdom.
Join Secure Code Warrior and help us in our mission to create a safer digital landscape. We’re empowering organizations to secure their software–no matter how the code is written!

The Technical Support Engineer role is technical and customer-facing. You'll own Level 1 and Level 2 support tickets from first response to resolution. You'll resolve platform issues across our Portal, SSO, API and integrations, and you'll triage content-related tickets with clear documentation so they reach the right people quickly. As your expertise grows, you'll take on our content ticket types (Challenges, Missions, Coding Labs, Quests, Courses and Tournaments) and start fixing straightforward content bugs yourself.

You'll work with customers around the world, explaining technical information clearly and helping them get the most from the platform. You'll also work with internal teams such as Customer Success, Sales, Engineering and Content. Together you'll resolve issues, spot bugs and improvement opportunities, and share them with the teams who can act on them.

What You Will Do

  • Diagnose, troubleshoot and resolve Level 1 and Level 2 tickets across the Portal, SSO, API and integrations.

  • Identify content-related tickets, resolve level 1 and level 2 issues. Reproduce and document any level 3 issues clearly before escalating to Senior Technical Support or the Content team.

  • Follow our triage, escalation and customer communication workflows, and use good judgment on when to involve Engineering.

  • Own SLA compliance on your tickets, and keep ticket management clean so every ticket shows an accurate, up-to-date status.

  • Ensure tickets are resolved according to timelines & priorities, and raising escalations when needed.

  • Maintain a "closed-loop" communication style so customers and internal teams always know where an issue stands.

  • Flag potential bugs and improvements with clear reproduction steps and pass them to the right teams.

  • Contribute to the knowledge base with articles for common platform issues.

  • Grow into handling content tickets independently and fixing straightforward content bugs directly.

What You Will Bring

  • 1+ years of experience in technical support or a customer-facing technical role, ideally in a SaaS environment.

  • Demonstrable programming knowledge, including the ability to read code and debug issues.

  • Familiarity with SSO (such as SAML and OIDC), REST APIs and third-party integrations is a strong plus.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.

  • Soft skills: empathy, a proactive approach, and a customer-focused mindset that keeps the customer experience at the center of every interaction.

  • Clear, confident written communication, especially when explaining technical issues to non-technical users.

  • Experience with software security would be a huge advantage but is not essential.

  • AI knowledge would be a huge benefit but is not essential, such as familiarity with AI coding assistants or how AI-generated code is created and reviewed.

  • A continuous-learning mindset and eagerness to grow your platform, content and security expertise.

  • A team player with a strong work ethic who takes ownership of your commitments.

You're joining us at an exciting stage of our journey, and you’re a key piece to what comes next. Expect real room to create impact and deliver on your ideas. The pace is quick and the bar is high; in return, you get genuine ownership and the kind of growth that only comes from building something that matters.

We also know you do your best work when you're rested and energized. Flexibility here runs on trust: we trust you to deliver when it counts, and we trust you to take the time you need to recharge. With teammates around the world, your hours can flex to fit your life, backed by generous leave and work-from-home options that help you make work work for you.

You'll join a tight-knit team that values humility and giving back, both to the community and to each other. Making the world a little brighter as we make it more secure is part of being a Warrior.

We live and work by the Warrior Code. It means getting feedback you can trust, shared without fear. It means no genius jerks: how you treat people counts as much as what you deliver. We do what we say we'll do, we celebrate the wins properly, and we do the right thing even when no one's watching. Come as you are, bring your best, and we'll do the same.

Position Summary
The Data Center New Build Deployment Enablement Manager (DEM) serves as the central coordination point for network infrastructure deployment at new data center builds — from cable start through Production Ready (PR). This role is "the glue" between Design, Engineering, Construction and Network Deployment teams and all cross-functional partners, ensuring milestones are tracked, dates are committed, and teams are aligned across every phase of the

network build.

The DEM heavily influences cross-functional teams to provide and commit to dates, serves as the single source of truth for deployment milestones, and drives accountability when timelines slip. This is not a passive tracking role — it requires deep technical fluency in Data Center network infrastructure, the ability to navigate complex multi-team political dynamics, and the confidence to escalate blockers to senior leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Milestone Coordination & Tracking
● Own and maintain the New Build Deployment Tracker for assigned buildings — tracking
milestones from Cable Ready to Production Ready (PR)
● Drive weekly New Build coordination calls with cross-functional and internal teams
● Track dependencies across multiple network layers
● Integrate with construction and network schedules and maintain alignment between multiple schedule sources

Cross-Functional Leadership & Communication
● Lead or co-lead New Build calls starting at cable start for data centers being built
● Post weekly program updates — highlighting new/changed risks, milestone
achievements, and upcoming milestone dates
● Serve as the bridge between Construction Managers, Deployment Engineers,
Connectivity Engineers, and all supporting teams
● Influence cross-functional partners to provide and commit to dates
● Facilitate SEV creation and escalation for schedule risks and cross-team blockers
Site Deployment Execution
● Coordinate network infrastructure deployment across multiple concurrent buildings (typically 2–4 simultaneous sites)
● Track hardware delivery SLAs, material logistics (warehouse locations, shipping from nearest facility), and upstream dependencies
● Understand and manage differences between building types
● Monitor and drive resolution of deployment blockers
Risk Management & Escalation

● Create and manage SEVs for deployment blockers
● Proactively communicate timeline impacts — provide specific information about expected impacts and revised timelines
● Escalate to leadership when cross-functional commitments are not being met
Process Development & Continuous Improvement

● Conduct lessons-learned reviews to identify recurring gaps in the deployment process
● Mentor and train incoming DEMs through reverse shadow model and milestone sessions

Required Skills & Qualifications

Technical & Domain Knowledge

● Proficiency with project tracking tools

simultaneously

● Direct experience with data center construction phases: foundation, cable start, TFO, commissioning, and network turn-up
● Experience working with MSPs (Managed Service Providers) and field operations teams in a data center environment
● Prior experience in hyperscale data center environments (Google, AWS, Microsoft, or similar) strongly preferred

● PMP, CAPM, or CSM certification preferred but not required

This is an individual contributor role with a primary focus on administering U.S. health & welfare programs and leaves of absence processes. This individual will work closely with Human Resources and Payroll to drive consistency and compliance in all benefit and leave-related matters.

Working with the Benefits leader, you will analyze current and proposed benefits programs for alignment with Enviri’s Total Rewards philosophy, market competitiveness, compliance with applicable regulatory and legislative requirements and for cost effectiveness.

You will be the primary liaison for employees in all divisions and corporate personnel, including the HR team, regarding escalated member issues (eligibility, coverage, claims, etc.). You'll work with vendor partners to ensure resolution of eligibility and claim issues, prepare accounting as needed for vendor remittance and reconcile employee contributions and partner with Payroll, HRIS and division HR teams to ensure smooth operation of plans and value-added employee experience.

This position will review and administer leave requests, including but not limited to Short- and Long-Term Disability, Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Parental Bonding Leave. You will provide assistance to and partner with vendor management, employees, human resources and business operations, develop and maintain various leave administration databases and spreadsheets, and track compliance and generate reports as requested.

This position may assist with and/or lead special projects as directed, and may prepare communication materials and conduct employee meetings/orientations for division HR teams as needed.

This is a remote position. Candidates must be based in the U.S. and able to work U.S. Eastern Time business hours.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

US Health & Welfare and LOA

  • Administer U.S. health & welfare programs and leave of absence processes across multiple vendors and systems, ensuring consistent application and operational continuity.
  • Manage end-to-end leave administration (FMLA, state leave, disability, workers’ compensation, paid parental), including case tracking, documentation, and employment status coordination.
  • First line contact with employees related to health & welfare benefits, leave and other benefits related questions.
  • Assist with the management of the U.S. Wellness program including biometric screenings, immunizations, health assessments and more.
  • Audit and monitor employee leave accrual banks and provide corrections and adjustments to Payroll.
  • Assist with the process for preparing, communicating, and tracking benefits related matters for collective bargaining agreements.
  • Prepare written employee communications, plan employee communication meetings and presentations.
  • Support Benefits Team and division HR Team on benefit-related matters and transactions that require intervention and interpretation. Ascertain appropriate resources and assist in resolution.
  • Communicate with employees, retirees, dependents and beneficiaries regarding eligibility, coverage, and other benefits matters.

Benefit, Payroll & Vendor Administration

  • Oversee benefits eligibility, enrollment, and payroll reconciliation.
  • Responsible for benefits invoicing processes.
  • Serve as primary operational liaison for external vendors supporting benefits and leave.
  • Assist with annual benefits open enrollment: coordinate internal and external resources to ensure system updates, communications, and all materials are accurately and timely distributed.
  • Support proxy-related reporting requirements.

Benefit Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with ACA, ERISA, CMS, PCORI and other related regulatory reporting requirements, supporting audit readiness across benefits and leave programs.
  • Maintain data integrity through reconciliation, reporting, and resolution of discrepancies across benefits, leave, payroll, and carrier systems.
  • Gather information for and assist with the Americans with Disabilities (ADA) Accommodation processes as needed.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Five or more years of progressive experience administering employee health and wellness benefit plans and leave administration.
    • Leave Administration regulations and processes with emphasis on FMLA administration and multi-state paid leave laws.
    • Benefit experience in large, public company to include self-insured/self-funded plans.
    • Experience with stoploss insurance, ERISA, HIPAA, ACA, and other legislative and compliance requirements.
    • Familiarity with retirement plans and collective bargaining agreements.
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication, organizational and analytical skills.
  • Ability to interact effectively with employees at all levels
  • Ability to maintain confidential information at all times.
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions
  • Ability to manage numerous initiatives to meet deadlines and to deliver high-quality outputs including the ability to re-order work and priorities.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret benefit plan documents, general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations.
  • Ability to write benefit communications, reports, business correspondence, and procedure documents in a clear and concise manner.
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from plan participants including active employees and retirees, as well as their dependents/beneficiaries and our vendor partners.
  • Ability to calculate figures and amounts to correct payroll deductions, invoices, and claims costs.
  • Ability to solve problems and partner effectively with internal and external teams.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.excerpt: Thanks for your interest in Oklo!  We are searching for a Director of Deployment Strategy and Integration to join our team.
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Director of Deployment Strategy and Integration to join our team.

Position Description

Oklo is hiring a Director of Deployment Strategy and Integration to serve as a high-judgment deputy to the Senior Director, Deployments. This senior, independent operator will own top-priority cross-functional deployment workstreams from problem framing and recommendation development through decision and implementation.

Deploying advanced nuclear technology requires technical, regulatory, commercial, financial, construction, schedule, operational, customer, and government considerations to move together, often before every fact is known. This leader will bring those inputs into a clear point of view, help senior leaders make consequential choices, and drive aligned teams through execution.

The Director will work across business units and functions, earning trust without relying on direct authority over every contributor. Success requires exceptional judgment and writing, comfort with ambiguity, a low-ego operating style, and the discipline to stay with the work until the outcome is real.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Own top-priority cross-functional deployment workstreams from problem definition through decision and implementation.
  • Enter ambiguous situations, identify the underlying question, and build a practical path to an answer.
  • Develop integrated recommendations that connect technical, commercial, regulatory, financial, construction, schedule, operational, customer, and government inputs.
  • Separate facts, assumptions, constraints, and preferences; test whether the available evidence supports the current plan.
  • Develop options with clear tradeoffs, second-order effects, owners, timing, and a recommended path.
  • Convene cross-functional teams, clarify interfaces, surface conflicts, and drive issues to closure or timely escalation.
  • Write concise decision memos, executive updates, meeting narratives, and implementation plans that stand on their own.
  • Represent the Senior Director, Deployments in defined meetings and workstreams and follow through on commitments within that mandate.
  • Convert lessons from live projects into practical, repeatable deployment practices for the broader portfolio.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Typically 10 or more years of relevant experience; demonstrated scope, judgment, and outcomes matter more than a specific number of years.
  • A record of independently leading complex, cross-functional work from an ambiguous starting point to a concrete outcome.
  • Strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior leaders and subject-matter experts without relying on reporting authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in clear, modern, active language.
  • The ability to learn technical and operational subject matter quickly and ask precise questions without overstepping domain expertise.
  • Experience carrying decisions into implementation and adapting as facts or conditions change.
  • The ability to operate with limited direction and represent a senior leader credibly within a defined mandate

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience leading complex programs, deployments, infrastructure development, strategy and operations, technical special projects, government programs, or high-stakes field operations.
  • Experience in advanced energy, nuclear, aerospace, defense technology, construction, industrial systems, autonomy, or another regulated hardware environment.
  • Familiarity with first-of-a-kind delivery, government customers or partners, complex contracts, project finance, capital decisions, stage gates, project controls, EPC partners, commissioning, or operational readiness.
  • Direct field, site, construction, manufacturing, or customer-deployment experience.

Competencies

We are looking for a Deployment Strategy and Integration Director that is:

  • A strong problem framer: Identifies the real decision, relevant time horizon, constraints, and downstream consequences before proposing a solution.
  • An independent decision-maker: Forms and defends a sound view with incomplete or conflicting information while being clear about uncertainty.
  • An exceptional writer: Turns a large, messy source set into a short document that an executive can use to decide and a team can use to act.
  • A systems thinker: Connects engineering, regulatory, commercial, finance, construction, schedule, operations, customer, and government realities without losing the critical path.
  • A decisive collaborator: Builds alignment across teams while keeping decision ownership clear and using escalation thoughtfully.
  • An execution-minded strategist: Converts recommendations into owners, sequence, resources, risks, and review points, and stays engaged through implementation.
  • Passionate about clean energy
  • Passionate about making advanced fission a reality
  • Willing and able to learn quickly
  • Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us
  • Willing to think differently and do things in new ways
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment
  • Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before
  • Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems
  • Able to communicate technical content and results verbally

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters in Santa Clara, California twice a quarter, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters. Travel is expected to be approximately 50% and may be higher during critical deployment periods, including travel to project sites and external stakeholder meetings.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $170,000-$220,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

The One Federation concept reinforces that as a strong, cohesive and collaborative Federation, we achieve significantly greater results for wildlife and people.

To support our mission, we are seeking to hire up to two Directors of Conservation Partnerships to join our One Federation team.

The Director of Conservation Partnerships (DCP) serves as a dynamic leader and strategist. This 360-degree role cultivates and maintains strong, trusted relationships both within NWF and across its affiliates and external partners, serving as a connector who strengthens communications, alignment and capacity for collaboration toward durable conservation outcomes. The role enables impactful partnerships between our national organization and state and territorial affiliates to achieve our shared vision as a cohesive conservation movement working at local, state, regional and national levels.

The Director of Conservation Partnerships reports to the Associate Vice President of Affiliate Partnerships and works closely with other DCPs and Affiliate Partnerships staff across the country, as well as national advocacy, program and development staff across NWF teams and departments.

Principal Duties

As a primary and mission critical relationship manager for NWF, and active and supportive partner to NWF staff, DCPs cultivate and maintain partnerships with a cohort of NWF affiliate organizations that drive collective Federation goals and outcomes. This position will be responsible for the following functions:

Federation Liaison

  • Serve as a bridge builder, ensuring two-way communication between NWF and its affiliates, bringing affiliate needs to national teams while actively integrating internal program teams into affiliate networks.
  • Connect affiliate staff directly to NWF subject-matter experts, scientific resources, federal policy teams to facilitate efficient and well-informed conservation advocacy.
  • Facilitate affiliate-to-affiliate partnerships. Connect affiliate leadership and staff to other affiliates to enable collaborative conservation initiatives and peer learning opportunities.
  • Proactively identify funding opportunities and national-state shared funding options to support collaborative initiatives and build long-term affiliate capacity.
  • Act as a force multiplier toward achieving conservation outcomes. Significantly increase effectiveness of affiliates and NWF through guiding and facilitating effective Federation collaboration by convening key stakeholders across NWF departments (e.g., policy, philanthropy, campaigns) and program teams to help co-design initiatives along with affiliates that meet both NWF and affiliate priorities.
  • Supporting or leading the convening of affiliates through regional, programmatic or operational opportunities including providing leadership for ad hoc or standing committees and work groups.

Thought Partner and Advisor

  • Serve as a trusted advisor and coach (where appropriate) to affiliate leaders, boards, and staff, offering input on executive management to ensure overall organizational health and resilience such as organizational and board development, strategic planning and prioritization, and financial management.
  • Help affiliate leaders and boards navigate sector standards, board governance norms, and organizational sustainability by providing best practices and capacity building opportunities.
  • Build trust, needs oversight, and alignment by maintaining a regular presence in the state as appropriate to each affiliate, attending virtual and in-person engagements such as staff, committee, and board meetings, public events, and relevant coalition and external partner meetings.
  • Facilitate relationships and communication lines between NWF board members and affiliates. Cultivate diverse NWF board recruitment pipelines through relationships with affiliates and partners. Ensure consistent affiliate participation in NWF governance and annual leadership meetings.

Organizational Growth Partner

  • Use an entrepreneurial mindset to enhance progress on affiliate priorities. Develop innovative approaches that ensure affiliates’ needs are met while increasing their capacity and prospecting for new opportunities to work jointly on areas of conservation need.
  • Work with affiliate and NWF leadership to address specific growth challenges, providing strategic consulting, as well as development and execution support where needed, on campaigns, fundraising, strategic planning, equity and justice integrations, and operational scaling.
  • Evaluate affiliate bandwidth before new program initiatives, grant awards, or sub-awards are finalized to ensure operational alignment and mitigation of performance risks.

Required Qualifications

Strong candidates for this position will have demonstrated proficiency in building and maintaining authentic partnerships with a diversity of individuals and organizations. Experience facilitating coalitions or networks is highly prized. Additionally, candidates are required to have:

  • Strong communication skills to ensure consistent, clear, and accessible lines of communication to all levels of organizations.
  • Experience working with nonprofit organizations and a depth of understanding of nonprofit governance, operations, communications, and fundraising principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage work independently and proactively identify opportunities and solutions.
  • Well-developed strategic thinking and prioritization skills and ability to balance multiple projects simultaneously.
  • A foundation in environmental, environmental justice, and/or conservation principles and practices through their educational background and/or professional experience in conservation, science, public policy or a related field.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

These proficiencies are typically consistent with at least ten years of professional experience.

Required Competencies

The individual selected for this role is expected to exemplify the National Wildlife Federation's core values – Work for Mission Impact, Act with Integrity, Collaborate Inclusively, Adapt Creatively, and demonstrate leadership competencies, including:

  • Executive-level emotional intelligence to navigate the complexities of multiple business relationships, governance structures, sensitive personnel challenges, and state-level political cultures.
  • Adaptability to customize relationship and support models to match the specific size, capacity, and maturity level of individual affiliates.
  • Conflict mediation and advocacy skills to serve as a buffer on policy push-pull dynamics while preserving affiliate autonomy and national alignment.
  • Being motivated by values of equity and responsibility to those most marginalized.
  • Consistently bringing a high level of empathy and social skills to team-oriented work and interpersonal interactions.
  • Actively seeking feedback, direction, and guidance from team members as well as keeping staff informed of decisions that impact them.
  • Passion for and commitment to NWF's mission and values.

Measures of Success

A DCP doesn't simply "support affiliates." They increase the effectiveness of the entire Federation by connecting people, information, expertise, resources, and opportunities. A DCP is successful when:

  • They embody the One Federation approach, live NWF’s values and are an ambassador of the entire Federation.
  • Their relationships are strong and built on trust and good two-way communication. They sustain productive relationships with affiliate leaders and staff, with affiliates experiencing the position as a responsive partner and valued advisor.
  • They successfully connect affiliate leaders and NWF staff with relevant national policy, program, fundraising, communications, and other subject-matter expertise to advance shared priorities.
  • They increase meaningful collaboration among affiliates and between affiliates and NWF teams, including the sharing of expertise, resources, strategies, relationships, and successful practices.
  • They identify and advance opportunities for affiliates and national teams to collaborate on fundraising, policy, programs, partnerships, communications, and other initiatives that advance shared objectives.
  • They contribute to stronger, more resilient, and more influential affiliates, including increased organizational capacity, strategic reach, partnerships, resources, and ability to advance conservation priorities within their states.
  • They increase the value and impact of working as a federation by identifying and facilitating opportunities where affiliates and the national organization can achieve greater results together than independently.
  • They serve as trusted thought partners and advisors to affiliate and NWF staff, providing informed perspective, facilitating problem-solving, and helping translate strategic priorities into effective action.
  • They strengthen collaboration and coordination across national teams by increasing understanding of affiliate priorities, capabilities, needs, and opportunities and reducing organizational silos that can impede effective partnership.
  • They contribute to a stronger, more connected Federation characterized by mutual trust, shared purpose, clear roles, effective communication, and alignment around organizational and conservation priorities.

Travel

Periodic travel to affiliates, national and/or regional meetings is expected. Anticipate 5-8 days every month, 30-60 nights per year.

Location and Work Mode

This position is fully remote; however, candidates must reside in or within an adjacent state to the Northeastern or Mid-Atlantic United States, within the geographic region extending from Maine to North Carolina. The National Wildlife Federation is committed to a flexible and empowered work environment with an authentic community of care for all staff.

Physical requirements:

Cognitive & Intellectual Requirements

  • Ability to understand, analyze, and apply complex information, policies, and concepts
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, problem-solve, and make decisions in situations involving ambiguity or competing priorities
  • Ability to maintain focus and sustained attention and manage multiple tasks or work-streams
  • Ability to listen, interpret, and respond appropriately in discussions with colleagues, leadership, and external stakeholders

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods of time while working at a computer or attending meetings
  • Ability to operate standard office equipment, including computers, keyboards, monitors, telephones, and video conferencing tools
  • Ability to communicate and exchange information in person, via telephone, and through electronic or virtual platforms
  • Ability to read, review, and produce written and electronic documents, including prolonged use of computer screens
  • Ability to move within an office or remote work environment to access files, meetings, or equipment as needed

Work Environment

  • Work is performed primarily in a remote environment.
  • Role may involve extended screen time and participation in virtual meetings.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this position is $85,000-$100,000 annually, commensurate with experience.

We are proud of our designation by Mogul as a Top 100 Workplace with the Best Benefits, and by Forbes as one of America’s best small employers! We value work-life balance and a family-friendly atmosphere with flexible scheduling. We want you to be able to integrate work and personal life with attention to your self-care, so that your work schedule is not depleting. We offer benefits so you feel restored and fueled through the day and week.

We offer these supports to help manage your mental, emotional, and physical health:

  • Paid time off: Vacation that starts off at three weeks accrual based on a full-time schedule, unlimited wellbeing (this time can be used for physical, spiritual, emotional, cultural, religious or financial wellbeing for yourself, a partner, or family member – including pets) half day Fridays, and 11 holidays
  • We close down for a paid winter break between December 25 to January 1 to recognize end of year stress, and time for reflection, rejuvenation, and spending time with family
  • Up to 16 weeks of fully paid Family and Medical Leave

  • Therapist available at no cost

In addition to your salary, we offer the following supports to your personal finances:

jobs.title: EU Proposal Writer & Funding Specialist
jobs.excerpt: AI2CYBER is looking for an experienced EU Proposal Writer & Funding Specialist to develop and coordinate funding proposals across cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies and defence research.
jobs.description:
AI2CYBER is looking for an experienced EU Proposal Writer & Funding Specialist to develop and coordinate funding proposals across cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies and defence research.

You will manage the proposal development process, from identifying suitable opportunities and shaping project concepts to coordinating partners, writing applications and completing submissions. You will work closely with our management, technical and finance teams to turn research ideas and product capabilities into credible, well-structured project proposals.

You will manage the proposal development process, from identifying suitable opportunities and shaping project concepts to coordinating partners, writing applications and completing submissions. You will work closely with our management, technical and finance teams to turn research ideas and product capabilities into credible, well-structured project proposals.

The role requires strong English writing skills, an understanding of cybersecurity, AI and quantum technologies, and knowledge of European funding programmes, including the European Defence Fund (EDF).

Requirements

  • Identify and assess relevant funding opportunities across Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, EDF, Eurostars and cascade funding calls, considering eligibility, strategic fit, resources and deadlines.
  • Analyse call documents, expected outcomes and evaluation criteria, and recommend opportunities aligned with the company’s capabilities and priorities.
  • Develop project concepts and write complete proposals, covering technical excellence, methodology, implementation, impact, exploitation and dissemination.
  • Work with technical specialists to describe the state of the art, explain the proposed innovation and define realistic use cases, validation activities and technology readiness levels.
  • Structure work packages, tasks, deliverables, milestones, performance indicators and risk management plans.
  • Identify potential partners, support consortium development and coordinate contributions from companies, research organisations and other stakeholders.
  • Prepare project budgets, effort allocations and supporting financial information in collaboration with the finance and technical teams.
  • Support EDF proposal preparation by reviewing call-specific requirements and coordinating eligibility, consortium and security-related checks with the relevant specialists.
  • Manage submission schedules, supporting documents and application platforms, checking completeness, consistency and compliance before submission.
  • Support clarification requests, grant preparation and the handover of successful proposals to the project delivery team.
  • Maintain proposal records and reusable material, analyse evaluation feedback and improve future submissions.

Benefits

  • Competitive remuneration, with periodic reviews.
  • Involvement in European research initiatives and challenging technology projects.
  • Professional development alongside experienced cybersecurity, AI and engineering specialists.
  • Access to learning materials and company resources.
  • The equipment and software needed to perform your role effectively.
  • An informal working environment without a prescribed dress code.

What We Are Looking For

  • Demonstrable experience writing and submitting European funding proposals, with clear personal responsibility for substantive sections or complete applications.
  • Excellent written English and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and persuasively.
  • Working knowledge of cybersecurity, including areas such as cyber threat intelligence, application security, vulnerability management, security operations and critical infrastructure protection.
  • Understanding of AI and machine learning concepts, including generative AI, intelligent automation, trustworthy AI and the security of AI systems.
  • Familiarity with quantum technologies and their security implications, particularly quantum computing, post-quantum cryptography and quantum-safe communications.
  • Knowledge of the European Defence Fund, including its research and development focus, call documentation, proposal requirements, evaluation approach and consortium considerations.
  • Ability to connect technical objectives with measurable outcomes, implementation plans, budgets and exploitation opportunities.
  • Strong research, organisational and stakeholder coordination skills, with the ability to manage parallel deadlines and maintain document quality.
  • Confidence working independently while actively seeking input and validation from technical and business colleagues.

Additional Experience We Would Value

  • A substantive contribution to proposals selected for funding, particularly in cybersecurity, AI, quantum technologies or defence.
  • Direct involvement in EDF proposal writing or consortium development.
  • Experience with defence research, dual-use technologies or collaboration with industrial partners and research institutions.
  • Familiarity with the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and other funding submission platforms.
  • Experience developing exploitation strategies, business cases, intellectual property approaches and commercialisation plans.
  • Experience supporting grant preparation, project reporting or technical deliverables after a funding award.

You will work directly with the people developing our technologies and delivering our services. This will give you access to the technical evidence, practical use cases and business priorities needed to build well-grounded proposals and contribute to our research and innovation direction.

About AI2CYBER

AI2CYBER develops cybersecurity technologies and provides specialist security services. Our work spans threat intelligence, application security, vulnerability discovery and automated security operations. We bring together cybersecurity expertise, artificial intelligence and software engineering to help organisations understand their exposure and address security weaknesses effectively.

The position is offered on a full-time basis.

Please email your CV in English to , using “EU Proposal Writer & Funding Specialist” as the subject line. Include a brief summary of relevant proposals, your specific contribution and your experience with cybersecurity, AI, quantum technologies and EDF. An anonymised writing sample is welcome where you have permission to share it.

We will handle your application confidentially.

jobs.description:
The Position

Title: Dean of Academic Excellence & Effectiveness

Position Type: Full-time

Requisition No: 27008

Category : Administration

Supervisor : VP of Learning and Instruction

Last Updated : July 2026

Job Purpose : This position leads Calbright's academic excellence and effectiveness agenda, advancing a

culture of continuous improvement, evidence-based practice, and accreditation integrity, while

helping drive cross-divisional systems, quality standards, and project management infrastructure

that support equitable student access, success, outcomes, and institutional growth.

Location: Remote, various locations throughout California

Salary Range: The beginning salary range for this position is Range M-21, (Steps 1-3) $159,314.04- $175,673.59.

**The first review of the application shall occur approximately on 10/12/2026**

Position Overview

The Dean of Academic Excellence & Effectiveness serves as an institutional leader and executive partner at Calbright College, providing strategic counsel and cross-functional guidance across program quality, institutional effectiveness, operations, accreditation, and college-wide initiatives. Working in close partnership with the VP of Learning and Instruction and the senior leadership team, the Dean plays a pivotal role in strengthening the quality and integrity of Calbright's academic programs and advancing a culture of evidence-based practice, continuous improvement, and equitable student success. The Dean serves as the College's primary Accreditation Liaison Officer (ALO) and works cross-functionally to strengthen institutional policies, procedures, and systems in alignment with accreditation standards, supporting all academic and non-academic functions in advancing Calbright's mission and growth. Success in this role requires a collaborative leader who is committed to evidence-based practice, equity, academic excellence, and the Calbright mission.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities

The duties below are representative of the role and are not intended to cover all of the duties performed within the scope of work.

Academic Quality and Effectiveness

  • Lead the College's academic program review cycle, guiding frameworks, timelines, and evidence-based program evaluation processes that drive continuous improvement.
  • Support the development, assessment, and revision of programs, advising on alignment with quality standards, accreditation needs, strategic priorities, and student success goals.
  • Provide strategic guidance on program optimization and processes, including program-level data analysis and evidence-based improvement recommendations across academic and non-academic units.
  • Collaborate with administration and cross-divisional teams to support operational systems, workflows, and reporting infrastructure that advance College effectiveness and embed data-informed decision-making at all levels.
  • Provide leadership and oversight of the College's industry Advisory Councils, guiding effective council governance, engagement, and cross-functional coordination, and collaborating with academic leaders to translate council input into actionable program improvements and workforce relevance.

Strategic Initiatives & Operations

  • Provide support, as needed, to the President and the senior leadership team on relevant institutional priorities, goals, organizational effectiveness, and emerging opportunities.
  • Support and facilitate institution-wide strategic initiatives, including organizational development, technology, culture and engagement efforts, effectiveness projects, and cross-divisional priorities aligned with the College's mission and strategic plan.
  • Guide and support the College's external advisory council engagement, helping advance industry alignment, employer partnerships, and program relevance across Calbright's workforce-focused portfolio.
  • Provide strategic planning, analysis, and advisory support to the VP of Learning and Instruction and senior leadership team, informing institutional priorities, goal-setting processes, and policy development.
  • Represent the College's effectiveness, quality, and innovation agenda externally where appropriate.

Project Management and Organizational Effectiveness

  • Provide leadership and oversight of L&I project managers and cross-functional project teams responsible for strategic and operational initiatives.
  • Establish project management standards, implementation timelines, and reporting processes to support successful project execution.
  • Monitor progress toward L&I goals, key performance indicators, and operational priorities, providing regular updates and recommendations to the VP.
  • Support the development of project evaluation processes that measure effectiveness, outcomes, and organizational impact.

Accreditation Leadership

  • Serve as the College's primary Accreditation Liaison Officer (ALO), maintaining effective communication and a productive institutional relationship with all accrediting agencies.
  • Guide and coordinate all accreditation cycles, including preparation of self-study evaluations, substantive and non-substantive change requests, program approvals, site visit coordination, and required follow-up reports.
  • Maintain current knowledge of evolving accreditation standards and regulations, advising team members on required institutional adjustments and strategic responses.
  • Help design and support internal review processes and cross-functional action plans that ensure ongoing standards compliance and a culture of continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate on the development and facilitation of professional development for faculty and staff on accreditation standards, processes, and institutional expectations.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong leadership, management, and organizational skills.
  • Strategic thinking and systems-level problem-solving, with a focus on continuous improvement, operational excellence, and equity-centered practice.
  • Knowledge of accreditation standards, institutional effectiveness practices, and continuous improvement frameworks in higher education.
  • Knowledge of higher education, curriculum development, instructional strategies, and/or assessment practices.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives amid competing priorities, with strong project management, implementation planning, and stakeholder coordination skills.
  • Knowledge of workforce development, labor market alignment, and/or employer engagement strategies.
  • Experience facilitating advisory groups, committees, councils, or stakeholder engagement processes.
  • Ability to analyze data, synthesize findings, prepare reports, and present actionable recommendations clearly and effectively.
  • Proficiency in using technology for data management, reporting, and communication.
  • Demonstrated understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, staff, and faculty.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree in education, administration, policy, or a related field.
  • At least five years of experience in higher education administration, with demonstrated leadership in institutional effectiveness, accreditation, academic quality, and/or strategic initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience leading accreditation processes and serving as a liaison to regional or national accrediting agencies.
  • Familiarity with online learning environments and quality standards related to distance education.
  • Proven track record of cross-functional leadership, project management, and driving institutional initiatives and operational improvement efforts across diverse stakeholder groups in higher education or a related sector.

Desired Qualifications

  • Doctorate in a related field.
  • Experience with both regional and specialized accreditation in higher education.
  • Experience in competency-based education, online education, workforce education, or innovative higher education models.
  • Experience presenting institutional effectiveness, accreditation, or project outcomes to governing boards, executive leadership teams, or external stakeholders.
  • Evidence of professional engagement and leadership in accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and/or strategic planning organizations.

Working Conditions and Travel

  • Calbright College is a statewide online college where all instruction and support are done via various online technologies both in person and remotely. Calbright College has administrative offices in Sacramento available for use. When working remotely, employees should be able and willing to use digital communication tools as used by the college and have the ability to work on a computer for extended periods of time. Although this is a primarily remote position, there may be instances in which you will be required to attend meetings or travel to in-person events.
  • Regular attendance is considered an essential job function; the inability to meet attendance requirements may preclude the employee from retaining employment.
  • The person holding this position is considered a mandated reporter under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements outlined in Calbright College policies, procedures, and Title IX.
  • Calbright College celebrates all forms of diversity and is deeply committed to fostering an inclusive environment within which students, staff, administrators,and faculty thrive. Individuals interested in advancing Calbright College’s strategic diversity goals are strongly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodations will be provided for qualified applicants with disabilities who self-disclose.
  • Requires the ability to function in a remote online instructional environment performing work of primarily a sedentary nature. Requires the ability to use hearing and speech to make presentations to groups and carry on conversations over the phone and in-person. Requires speaking skills to communicate with staff and students in one-on-one and small group settings, on the phone, and to distinguish sound prompts from various types of equipment. Requires near visual acuity to read printed materials and computer screens. Requires sufficient hand/arm/finger dexterity to retrieve work materials, operate a personal computer keyboard, and operate standard office equipment. Requires the ability to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
  • Work is performed indoors where minimal safety considerations exist.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Calbright College provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Calbright College complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

Who We Are

Calbright College is one of California’s newest community colleges – the first statewide, online campus designed to bridge the gap between employers with unfilled positions and students who don’t have either the time or money to attend a traditional school. Our mission is to increase economic mobility and close equity gaps for working adults who lack easy access to traditional forms of higher education by offering online, flexible, affordable skills-based programs that provide tangible economic value for both working adults and hiring managers.

Salary: $159,314.04- $175,673.59
