jobs.description:
About Rediminds

At RediMinds, we build AI-enabled systems that help complex industries operate better, faster, and more intelligently. Our work spans healthcare, legal, finance, government, and other high-impact domains where software quality, trust, and speed truly matter.

We are a growing, entrepreneurial team that values ownership, clarity, compassion, and technical excellence. We're looking for builders who want to grow with us, contribute meaningfully, and be part of a team creating real products with real-world impact.

RediMinds — building the future with people who care enough to get the details right.

RediMinds, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Contractor. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all contractors and applicants and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for contract without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws

100% Remote | Full-Time | Contract-to-Hire

The opportunity

Every independent review represents a person seeking access to care or essential services. At RediMinds, we combine technology-enabled workflows with the judgment of independent clinicians to help deliver fair, well-supported, and timely determinations.

We are adding Case Review Managers to safeguard quality at two critical points: when a case enters our system and before the final determination is issued. Much of the administrative workflow is automated. Your judgment, attention to detail, and clear writing ensure the information is right, discrepancies are resolved, and each determination is complete and ready for release.

What you will do

  • Review incoming case files for completeness and accuracy, including case summaries, member and service details, clinical records, supporting documents, and key dates; identify missing or inconsistent information.
  • Validate system-generated summaries and case information against the underlying record, escalating discrepancies and ensuring a reliable foundation for clinician review.
  • Quality-check clinicians’ written reviews for completeness, internal consistency, clear rationale, accurate references to supporting evidence, and responsiveness to the question under review.
  • Work directly with clinicians to clarify or correct gaps in documentation while preserving their independent clinical judgment and decision-making authority.
  • Perform final quality assurance on determination letters, ensuring they faithfully reflect the clinician’s findings, are clear and professional, and meet applicable case-specific requirements before issuance.
  • Coordinate with clinical and operations teams to resolve issues, maintain accurate case records, and meet standard and expedited review deadlines.
  • Protect confidential health information, follow independence and conflict-of-interest safeguards, and identify opportunities to strengthen quality and improve workflows.

What you bring - required

  • Hands-on experience in utilization review (UR), healthcare appeals, independent review, clinical review operations, or closely related medical-record and decision-document quality assurance.
  • Ability to read and critically assess clinical documentation, identify omissions or inconsistencies, and raise well-founded questions for the appropriate clinical reviewer.
  • Excellent written communication and editing skills; able to make complex, sensitive determinations clear, accurate, and consistent.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple cases against firm deadlines.
  • Comfort working in technology-enabled systems and independently verifying summaries, documents, and other system outputs against source records.
  • Understanding of patient confidentiality and the importance of impartial, well-documented healthcare review processes.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a healthcare-related field or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

Especially valuable - not required

  • Direct experience with an Independent Review Organization (IRO), external grievance reviews, or external healthcare appeals.
  • Experience with Pennsylvania Personal Assistance Services (PAS) cases is especially valuable; related experience in Community HealthChoices, Medicaid managed care, or long-term services and supports (LTSS) is also welcome.
  • Experience auditing clinical review rationales and final determination or appeal letters for quality and regulatory completeness.
  • A clinical credential (such as RN or LPN/LVN) or relevant clinical training.

How we work

This is a fully remote, self-directed role with close collaboration across clinical and operations teams. Evening or weekend work may be required when needed to meet regulatory deadlines. The Case Review Manager is accountable for documentation and process quality; independent clinicians remain responsible for clinical determinations.

jobs.description:
THE POSITION:

The Project Accountant, Deployment Billing and Contract Revenue, will support Deployment billing, contract administration, revenue recognition, deferred revenue review, and project setup activities for complex client contracts. This role will analyze Statements of Work, amendments, pricing exhibits, and billing provisions to ensure contract terms are translated into accurate project setup, billing requirements, revenue treatment, and recurring operational controls. The position will partner with Project Accounting, Deployment Operations, Sales Operations, FP&A, HR, Payroll, Talent Acquisition, Legal / Contract Management, and IT / Power Platform resources to improve billing readiness, reduce key-person dependency, and strengthen revenue integrity.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams. These results are achieved by:

  • Review SOWs, amendments, pricing schedules, rate cards, and related contract documents to identify billing-relevant terms, required data inputs, approval requirements, exceptions, and renewal or escalation provisions.
  • Translate contract terms into billing requirements, project setup instructions, recurring invoice support needs, revenue recognition considerations, deferred revenue requirements, and audit support documentation.
  • Apply accounting judgment and working knowledge of ASC 606 revenue recognition concepts to support appropriate revenue treatment, including identification of performance obligations, timing of revenue recognition, variable consideration, contract modifications, and required documentation.
  • Support deferred revenue analysis, reconciliations, release schedules, and period-end review to ensure revenue is recognized in accordance with contract terms, company policy, and applicable accounting guidance.
  • Create, maintain, and validate project setup information in D365 or related ERP systems, including project contracts, project IDs, billing rules, funding sources, contract lines, invoice formats, rate structures, and required billing metadata.
  • Partner with business owners to obtain required operational inputs, including rosters, vacancies, hires, terminations, recruiting activity, salary information, bonus activity, cost model assumptions, amendments, and CRM updates.
  • Maintain contract terms registers, billing requirements trackers, responsibility assignments, approval records, issue logs, and supporting documentation.
  • Prepare or support monthly and quarterly billing, revenue, deferred revenue, accrual, reconciliation, and close activities related to Deployment contracts.
  • Research and resolve contract interpretation, billing setup, invoice support, revenue recognition, and data ownership issues in collaboration with Finance, Operations, Legal, Sales Operations, HR, Payroll, FP&A, and IT.
  • Support process documentation, template development, testing, training materials, and continuous improvement efforts related to Deployment billing readiness and contract term management.

At Advarra, we are passionate about making a difference in the world of clinical research and advancing human health. With a rich history rooted in ethical review services combined with innovative technology solutions and deep industry expertise, we are at the forefront of industry change. A market leader and pioneer, Advarra breaks the silos that impede clinical research, aligning patients, sites, sponsors, and CROs in a connected ecosystem to accelerate trials.

Company Culture

Our employees are the heart of Advarra. They are the key to our success and the driving force behind our mission and vision. Our values (Patient-Centric, Ethical, Quality Focused, Collaborative) guide our actions and decisions. Knowing the impact of our work on trial participants and patients, we act with urgency and purpose to advance clinical research so that people can live happier, healthier lives.

At Advarra, we seek to foster an inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone is treated with respect and diverse perspectives are embraced. Treating one another, our clients, and clinical trial participants with empathy and care are key tenets of our culture at Advarra; we are committed to creating a workplace where each employee is not only valued but empowered to thrive and make a meaningful impact.

Job Overview Summary

Advarra has as its core function the institutional review board (IRB) review of all human subject’s research from survey research to first-in-human research sponsored by pharmaceutical companies, biotech companies, institutions, hospitals as well as clinics and private physician offices. Within the IRB, the regulatory department is responsible for the expedited review of research, the full board review of research and the drafting and writing of the meeting minutes. The regulatory department also collaborates with other parts of the organization on thought leadership, client guidance, and operational efficiencies.

Affiliated Board Members (ABM) are full-time Advarra employee board members who conduct IRB reviews on behalf of the organization. Based on educational background, experience, and expertise ABMs can be designated as either scientific or non-scientific and workload is distributed accordingly. A non-scientific ABM is a board member who does not have a scientific educational background or significant professional experience in a scientific field but has a strong understanding of research regulations and guidance.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

  • Maintain superior level knowledge of, and ensure Review Board compliance with, regulatory requirements, Advarra’s Board Standard Operating Procedures and Organizational Policies and Procedures. Help ensure the timely execution of the core review activities of the Institutional Review Board, while preserving the highest quality of professionalism and regulatory compliance
  • Be a resource to answer questions and help to solve day-to-day challenges whether in collaboration with Advarra staff or other board members
  • Assist as necessary with the triaging and review of submissions for expedited or full board review
  • Attend full board meetings and present protocol related issues as needed
  • Identify to senior regulatory staff areas that would benefit from guidance, inconsistencies in Board reviews, and other like issues
  • Consult, as necessary, with sponsors, investigators, CROs on clinical and regulatory affairs
  • Work with Regulatory Leadership to identify membership needs and to help develop Board members to ensure consistency of Review Board related activities
  • Enhance and encourage a work atmosphere centered on accountability through motivation, team building, training, mentoring, collaboration, and respect to create a highly efficient and successful workplace

Location

This role is open to candidates working remotely in the United States.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree
  • One (1)+ years of IRB or Clinical Research Industry experience preferred, OR minimum 3 years’ experience in healthcare within the last 6 years

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s Degree
  • Certified IRB Professional (CIP) certification

Physical and Mental Requirements

  • Sit or stand for extended periods of time at stationary workstation
  • Regularly carry, raise, and lower objects of up to 10 Lbs.
  • Learn and comprehend basic instructions
  • Focus and attention to tasks and responsibilities
  • Verbal communication; listening and understanding, responding, and speaking

jobs.description:
EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND HEALTH BOARD

First Things First (FTF) is an essential leader and partner in creating a family-centered, equitable, high-quality early childhood system that supports the development, well-being, health and education of all Arizona’s children, birth to age 5. Created by voter initiative in 2006, FTF is governed by a state Board with 28 regional partnership councils. First Things First is a decentralized organization that engages diverse constituencies to accomplish its mission. Organizational values include a commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion; a focus on accountability, transparency, coordination and collaboration; and an emphasis on improving outcomes that will ensure young children start kindergarten healthy and ready to succeed in school and in life.

First Things First values its government-to-government relationships with tribes in Arizona. Tribes can participate in First Things First in one of two ways: by electing to have their tribal lands treated as separate regions by the statewide FTF Board, or by electing to have their tribal lands treated as part of the FTF regions in which their lands are geographically located. To date, 19 federally recognized tribes have elected to participate in First Things First (10 as separate regions, and nine as part of the region in their geographic area). The Gila River Indian Community and Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community are located within the Phoenix Regional Area.

Administrative Specialist III

Job Location:

Address: 4000 N Central Avenue, Suite 500, Phoenix, AZ 85012

Posting Details:

Salary: $47,840

Grade: 17

Job Summary:

The Administrative Specialist III (ASIII) position serves as the central coordinator for the Phoenix Regional Area including administrative support for the four regions: Phoenix North, Phoenix South, Gila River Indian Community and Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community and assists the Phoenix Regional Area Director. A key function of this position is to provide active support to the four regional partnership councils, each comprising 11 volunteer community members, ensuring that meetings comply with the legal obligations established for First Things First. This position is an integral part of a team-based environment, providing a variety of complex administrative activities as well as being part of a culture that offers exemplary customer service. The ASIII serves as an ambassador and trustworthy representative of First Things First, coordinating work with regional staff, regional council members and ensuring effective communication with internal colleagues and external community partners. This position also has the opportunity to work as an active and contributing member of multiple teams, including working professionally and effectively with other administrative specialists to develop increased efficiencies in administrative work.

This position may offer the ability to work remotely, within Arizona, based upon the department's business needs and continual meeting of expected performance measures.

The State of Arizona strives for a work culture that affords employees flexibility, autonomy, and trust. Across our many agencies, boards, and commissions, many State employees participate in the State’s Remote Work Program and are able to work remotely in their homes, in offices, and in hoteling spaces. All work, including remote work, should be performed within Arizona unless an exception is properly authorized in advance.

Job Duties:
  • Administratively support staff and volunteer regional council members.
    ○ Examples of staff support include the Phoenix Regional Area Director and the regional specialists. Includes directly reporting to the Phoenix Regional Area Director.
    ○ Examples of support include calendar management, reimbursement and travel management, coordination of regional council meeting logistics (includes virtual and in-person formats) and meeting document preparation such as meeting packets, recording and retaining meeting minutes, etc. in adherence with Open Meeting Law.
    ● Project manager and leader for multiple/simultaneous administrative responsibilities.
    ○ Examples include regional area budget and procurement monitoring, office management, records retention, file management, state vehicle management and cross-regional collaboration activities.
    ○ Proficient in communicating using multiple modalities, including email, instant messaging, phone and text.
    ○ Process applications and related paperwork using a web-based platform for volunteer regional council members and support the member onboarding process while maintaining strict confidentiality of all information.
    ○ Examples of regional council member support include coordinating interview processes, onboarding and off boarding process, including training and paperwork and maintaining the regional council member database.
    ○ Coordinate, prepare and process travel-related activities and reimbursements for regional staff and regional council members.
    ○ Assist with the request for grant application process in alignment with Arizona State Procurement procedures, including accepting requests for grant application proposals from applicants, coordinating applicable meetings related to the confidential review process and assisting with the mailing and delivery of applications.
    ○ Serve as a subject matter expert and support to staff in Open Meeting Law, conflict of interest and computer applications such as Adobe Acrobat Pro, SharePoint, Google Workspace and virtual meeting applications.
    ● Onboarding and training new staff, such as a regional specialist in administrative processes and procedures. The position may serve as an interim support to other regions when necessary.

● Leading quality improvement practices

○ Examples include initiating and leading workgroups to create, review and update administrative procedures to promote efficiencies within the organization. Accurately and timely communicating changes for the target audience.
● Participation in and/or leading discussions and regional area team meetings with other administrative specialists throughout the regional area and/or state.
● Performs duties in a manner that supports the First Things First internal culture and mission with respect and cooperation.
● Supports additional opportunities as related to the role and regional team functions.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities (KSAs):
  • At least four years of administrative experience working in a team environment; or a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in a relevant field with at least two years of administrative experience working in a team environment.
    ● Evidence of strong oral, written and listening communication skills, including editing and formatting documents and demonstrating excellent writing skills. Experience in developing and maintaining email distribution lists.
    ● Possess strong, current computer skills in Adobe Acrobat Pro; Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat, Gmail, Meet and Sites); and Microsoft Office (SharePoint, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Publisher) and virtual meeting applications.
    ● Extensive organizational and time management skills, experience with project management processes, ability to handle multiple projects and adjust priorities to meet deadlines.
    ● Previous experience in offering exemplary customer service within the communities within the Phoenix Regional Area is strongly preferred.
    ● Experience with minute-taking and writing. Maintaining record retention of documents in accordance with Open Meeting Law is preferred. Knowledge of Arizona Open Meeting Law and experience working with a community group of volunteers, board or council is preferred.
    ● Flexibility in work schedule, such as an occasional meeting that occurs during the evening and/or weekend hours.
    ● Ability to travel, including overnight stays. This remote position also requires regular in-person participation at meetings held outside the immediate service area.

jobs.description:
What’s up? We’re VaynerMedia! We are a contemporary global creative and media agency with an expertise in driving relevance for clients and delivering impactful business results. The independently-owned agency was founded in 2009 and has offices in New York, Los Angeles, London, Singapore, Australia, Thailand, Japan and Mexico City. VaynerMedia has been recognized for its work at Cannes Lions, the Clio Awards and The Webby Awards. It is part of the VaynerX family of companies.

Culture is our key and Empathy is how we build it. VaynerMediaAPAC is strong with a world-class combination of diverse backgrounds collaborating to put forward innovative, creative and strategic solutions to the one advantage that stands the test of time --- PEOPLE. Day in and day out, we propel some of the biggest brands in the world to the intersection of attention and culture. In APAC, we are proudly +200, servicing a diverse client all around the region.

The PITCH

We’re lucky that everyone within our walls thinks creatively, shares a passion for building communities, and understands the world of both big campaigns and social micro-content.

Do you feel like you live and breathe social media? Know all the different Gen Z lingos and trends? Or have an undying need to check Twitter every five minutes? Oh well, we are meant to be ---

Here’s where you come in.

  • Ultimate team player who will create value in any situation.
  • Flawlessly understands creative problem solving and has a passion for storytelling on every platform.
  • Adaptable idea person who understands that good ideas can come from anywhere, and have the ability to guide a brainstorm.
  • Obsessed in being highly observant and writing because you love to.
  • Execute quickly and manage your time well.
  • Aware of your strengths and your weaknesses.
  • You’re cool in the face of a challenge.
  • You'll be working exclusively within the digital realm (no print work,) so the portfolio you submit should reflect this. However, we also love seeing your overall solutions and ideas throughout your book.

Here’s the Gig --

  • Do a range of creative work from faster, “smaller” pieces of content to “bigger” builds for a range of clients, as well as VaynerMedia-wide projects
  • Work within a dynamic team structure with several creative leads, helping to support and deliver on our core community and brand specific campaigns
  • Mastery of industry best practices and the platforms we love, as well as be willing to learn and articulate the unique VaynerMedia POV on each
  • Care more about concepting, writing, developing, and putting the team in the best position to present our ideas than you do about getting credit for the work
  • Be a friendly teacher as a proficient doer when working within our Creative team structure.
  • Strong storytelling skills and a mastery of grammar and the Japanese language.

Your Experience

  • Passion for social media and all things social
  • Mastery of the Japanese language and possess a strong desire to write good things
  • Conceptual and brainstorming skills
  • Time management, organization, and communication
  • Effectively collaborate with various teams, providing useful guidance in an enthusiastic and inspiring manner
  • Keen interest in the big social media platforms and their abilities/limitations
  • Experience working with designers, developers, and team focused creative process
  • An obsession with sports, music, or food-we love people who can bring their own interests into the mix

What you should know about VaynerMedia

Think “lab” and not “agency”. We get excited about solving business problems, not creating advertising for the sake of making advertising. Our entrepreneurship DNA runs deep. We’re willing to break rules, try new things, and test hypotheses if it means better understanding our craft. It’s fun!

Our environment (and pace) feels much more like a start-up than most agencies you might be used to. Hopefully that, and the opportunity to collaborate with the talented and enthusiastic crew, work with big brands excites you, as it does us. We can’t wait to meet you.

P.S Send us your portfolio --- always excited to see some unicorn talents :)

🤙🏼 About gaiia

At gaiia, we're building the leading platform for Communications Service Providers (CSPs) that truly care about their customers. Our core product is an operating system (OS) for telcos that manages billing, operations, automation and everything in between.

We're passionate about taking care of our people, and it's not just lip service. We want you to focus on your job while we care for everything else. We offer competitive pay and benefits, attractive stock options, unparalleled transparency, and a 100% remote environment. We're excited to have you join us for your next career adventure!

🎭 Role & Team

We're looking to hire a Senior Security Engineer with excellent technical skills, strong security judgment, and effective communication skills.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can operate as both a security generalist and a strong full-stack engineer. You will help protect gaiia’s products, infrastructure, customers, and teams by combining deep technical execution with pragmatic security leadership.

You will report to the Platform Lead and work closely with the Platform Lead and the CTO as thought partners. Together, you will help identify, prioritize, and execute the most important security work based on business criticality, customer impact, risk, and operational urgency.

This role is ideal for someone who can move fluidly between code, cloud infrastructure, product architecture, incident response, compliance, and team enablement, while staying grounded in practical business outcomes.

📽 What is your team working on?

Technically speaking, you will work in a serverless ecosystem of microservices deployed on a cloud infrastructure. Gaiia is all-in on Typescript, with frontend, backend and infrastructure-as-code all leveraging Typescript.

As part of the security function, you will have the chance to work across five major axes:

Product and application security

Protect gaiia’s products and customer-facing workflows by building security into design, development, testing, and remediation.

  • Perform threat modelling and architecture reviews.
  • Review authentication, authorization, tenant isolation and sensitive workflows.
  • Review our secure-development standards and lightweight security reviews.
  • Run internal penetration tests and work with developers on labelling issues and implementing remediations.
  • Build and maintain a bug bounty program.

Cloud and infrastructure security

Strengthen the security of our cloud platforms, production environments, access model, deployment pipelines, and critical vendor configurations.

  • Review AWS, Snowflake, GitHub and other critical vendors’ configurations.
  • Improve IAM, least privilege and production access for employees.
  • Improve IAM, least privilege and production access for Lambdas and other cloud resources.
  • Review logging, detection and cloud-security monitoring.
  • Review infrastructure-as-code and deployment pipelines.
  • Harden data stores, networks, backups and encryption controls.

Vulnerability and incident management

Create a clear operating model for finding, prioritizing, investigating, remediating, and learning from security issues and incidents.

  • Own vulnerability intake, prioritization and remediation SLAs.
  • Track root causes and ensure corrective actions are completed and satisfactory.
  • Triage security alerts and coordinate investigations.
  • Maintain incident-response plans and conduct exercises.
  • Document escalation and communication procedures.

Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC)

Maintain the policies, controls, evidence, and customer-facing security posture needed to meet regulatory, audit, sales, and legal expectations.

  • Participate in the review and operation of current programs, including SOC 2, GDPR, and PCI.
  • Coordinate auditors and external assessments.
  • Help the Sales team with security questionnaires that they cannot answer confidently.
  • Support the CTO in sales and legal negotiations involving security commitments.
  • Review vendors and subprocessors’ security controls.

Security enablement

Scale security across the company through training, guardrails, champions, roadmap planning, and leadership visibility.

  • Build and enforce training for engineering and employees.
  • Build reusable guardrails that scale without manually approving everything.
  • Establish security champions across Engineering to aid in security initiatives.
  • Maintain a prioritized security roadmap.
  • Report material risks and progress to leadership.
  • Participate in the long-term plan to build the security team.

🎖️ Qualifications

Technical

  • At least five (5) years of experience in Software Engineering, Application Security, Infrastructure Security, or a closely related technical role.
  • Strong experience securing modern web applications, APIs, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure.
  • Strong experience with AWS.
  • Strong experience with the JavaScript / TypeScript ecosystem.
  • Experience with React.
  • Experience working with microservices, serverless architectures, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines, and production systems.
  • Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, secrets management, IAM, logging, monitoring, and secure SDLC practices.
  • Experience with penetration testing, bug bounty programs, SAST, dependency scanning, etc.

Personal

  • Stellar judgement and pragmatism when making and implementing critical business decisions.
  • Rigorous, calm, and level-headed approach to incidents, ambiguity, and high-stakes situations.
  • Impressive communication skills, with the ability to coach, influence, and enable teams without slowing them down unnecessarily.
  • Ability to prioritize security work based on business impact, customer risk, operational urgency, and engineering feasibility.
  • Experience reviewing product architecture, identifying practical security risks, and partnering with engineering teams to implement effective mitigations.

🪄 Nice-to-haves

  • You have experience with GraphQL.
  • You have knowledge of telecom concepts.
  • You have experience working on a System of Record.
  • You have experience with compliance programs.
  • You have experience supporting sales and legal conversations involving security commitments.

At gaiia, we have a transparent salary philosophy and a robust evaluation and compensation framework. It translates to a fair and impartial model where salaries are published internally, healthy discussions around compensation and performance can exist, and taboos are removed.

Rollen som IT-arkitekt inom Sussa vårdstöd är central för att säkerställa att tjänsteleveransen möter regionernas behov. Du har därmed en viktig och ansvarsfull uppgift i att skapa en sammanhållen och framtidssäkrad arkitektur som stödjer samtliga regioners vårdverksamheter.

I rollen som IT-arkitekt inom Sussa vårdstöd arbetar du främst med att etablera, förvalta och säkerställa efterlevnad av nödvändiga styrmekanismer, exempelvis arkitekturprinciper och målarkitekturer. Du verkar även för att Sussa-regionerna erhåller en hållbar, förvaltningsbar och kostnadseffektiv tjänsteleverans.

Du stöttar regionerna i att vidareutveckla den övergripande arkitekturen utifrån Sussa-regionernas behov.

Inom ramen för Sussa vårdstöd arbetar du bland annat med att:

  • Leda och samordna det övergripande arkitekturarbetet.

  • Vara ordförande och sammankallande för forumen: - Sussa vårdstöd – Region - Arkitekturforum - Sussa vårdstöd – Region - Lösningsarkitekturforum

  • Representera Sussa vårdstöd i forum och möten som drivs av andra organisationer och myndigheter, exempelvis Inera, SKR och E-hälsomyndigheten

  • Fungera som strategiskt stöd till objektägare och objektägare IT för Sussa vårdstöd

  • Delta i arbetet med tjänsteutveckling på både strategisk och taktisk nivå

  • Driva framtagandet av målbilder och målarkitekturer för Sussa samverkan

  • Omvärldsbevaka utveckling och trender inom arkitekturområdet och digitalisering av hälso- och sjukvården

  • Hålla samman den övergripande arkitekturen inom perspektiven verksamhetsarkitektur, informationsarkitektur, applikationsarkitektur, infrastrukturarkitektur och säkerhetsarkitektur

  • God kunskap om modeller, metoder och ramverk som används inom lösnings- och enterprisearkitektur.

Job Title: Clinical Product Research Analyst
Location: Remote | United States
EmploymentType: Full-Time | Temporary Contract | 1099 Independent Contractor or Temporary Employee
Department: Clinical Product Research / Healthcare Supply Chain / Product Analysis
ContractDuration: Approximately 6 Months
Schedule: Monday–Friday | Core Business Hours Generally 8:00 AM–5:00 PM | Some Scheduling Flexibility
WeeklyHours: Approximately 40 Hours
PayRate: $45 - $55/per hour | Higher Rates May Be Considered Based on Relevant Experience and Supporting Compensation History
ClinicalFocus: General Medical, Critical Care, Acute Care, Inpatient, and Ambulatory Care Products


Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced and highly analytical Clinical Product Research Analyst to support healthcare product research, clinical product evaluations, and functional equivalency assessments in a fully remote, six-month contract position.

In this role, you will leverage your hands-on clinical experience and knowledge of medical supplies, equipment, and patient care products to evaluate products across multiple manufacturers and determine whether they are clinically appropriate alternatives for specific healthcare applications. You will work alongside a team of analysts and healthcare supply chain professionals to review extensive product lists, compare technical specifications, validate clinical applications, and develop evidence-based recommendations that support product sourcing, standardization, and conversion initiatives.

This opportunity is ideal for an experienced clinical professional, such as an ICU Nurse, Emergency Department Nurse, Medical-Surgical Nurse, Respiratory Therapist, Clinical Product Specialist, or Value Analysis Professional, who wants to apply their clinical expertise in a research-focused capacity without providing direct patient care. The position offers 100% remote work, a flexible daytime schedule, and the opportunity to influence healthcare product selection and standardization decisions across a wide range of clinical environments.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Product Research & Evaluation

  • Research and evaluate medical supplies, clinical equipment, and patient care products used across general medical, critical care, acute care, inpatient, and ambulatory healthcare settings.
  • Review extensive product lists developed by internal analysts to determine clinical suitability, appropriate applications, and potential product alternatives.
  • Conduct functional equivalency assessments to determine whether products from different manufacturers can appropriately serve the same clinical purpose.
  • Compare product specifications, intended use, performance characteristics, clinical applications, and manufacturer documentation.
  • Apply practical clinical knowledge to evaluate how products are used in real-world patient care environments.
  • Identify clinically meaningful differences between competing products, including potential impacts on patient safety, workflows, treatment effectiveness, and product usability.
  • Distinguish critical clinical differences from minor variations that do not materially affect product functionality.
  • Evaluate available technical documentation, clinical evidence, regulatory information, and manufacturer specifications to validate product recommendations.
  • Research and compare products from multiple manufacturers while maintaining objective, unbiased evaluations.
  • Identify potential limitations, contraindications, or clinical concerns associated with proposed product substitutions.
  • Develop evidence-based recommendations regarding product equivalency, clinical appropriateness, and potential replacement options.

Product Categories & Clinical Applications

Support research and product comparisons involving categories such as:

  • General Medical and Patient Care Consumables
  • Critical Care and Emergency Department Supplies
  • Medical-Surgical and Acute Care Products
  • Vascular Access Products
  • Infusion Therapy Products
  • Wound Care and Dressing Supplies
  • Infection Prevention Products
  • Respiratory Care Products
  • Enteral Nutrition Products
  • Urology Products
  • Ostomy and Continence Care Supplies
  • Women's Health and Labor & Delivery Products
  • Neonatal Care Products
  • Renal and Dialysis Products
  • Oncology Products
  • Patient Monitoring Accessories
  • General Clinical Supplies and Equipment

Candidates are not expected to be experts in every product category, but should possess broad clinical product knowledge and the ability to research unfamiliar products effectively.

Data Analysis & Product Documentation

  • Analyze large product datasets containing hundreds to thousands of medical product records.
  • Use advanced Microsoft Excel functions to organize, compare, validate, and analyze product information.
  • Perform product matching and cross-referencing using XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, Pivot Tables, sorting, filtering, and data validation tools.
  • Identify inconsistencies, missing information, duplicate records, and discrepancies within product databases.
  • Research incomplete or conflicting product information using multiple reliable sources.
  • Maintain accurate product cross-reference databases and structured research documentation.
  • Document product characteristics, clinical applications, functional similarities, and clinically relevant differences.
  • Support the development of an internal clinical product knowledge database designed to capture product equivalencies and research findings for future reference.
  • Ensure research findings are consistent, accurate, traceable, and supported by appropriate documentation.
  • Develop clear written summaries explaining product comparisons and the clinical rationale behind recommendations.

Supply Chain Collaboration & Research Support

  • Collaborate with healthcare supply chain professionals, clinical stakeholders, and internal research analysts to support product evaluation initiatives.
  • Assist with medical product standardization, sourcing, contract conversions, and product substitution projects.
  • Provide clinical insight regarding product utilization, operational considerations, and potential impacts of product changes.
  • Respond to questions regarding product research findings and explain the evidence supporting clinical recommendations.
  • Participate in occasional project meetings to discuss research progress, findings, and outstanding product questions.
  • Work independently to complete assigned research projects within established timelines.
  • Maintain consistent productivity, attention to detail, and research quality in a remote work environment.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Education: Relevant clinical education, healthcare training, or professional background demonstrating practical knowledge of medical products and their clinical applications.
  • Clinical Experience: Strong, relatively recent hands-on clinical experience or practical clinical product expertise in general medical, critical care, acute care, inpatient, ambulatory care, or related healthcare environments.
  • Clinical Product Knowledge: Demonstrated understanding of medical supplies, equipment, and products commonly used in patient care.
  • Practical Experience: Must have experience utilizing, supporting, evaluating, educating others about, or researching medical products in healthcare delivery environments.
  • Product Evaluation: Ability to assess the clinical appropriateness of medical products and identify suitable alternatives based on intended use, functionality, and patient care requirements.
  • Multi-Manufacturer Knowledge: Familiarity with products from multiple manufacturers and the ability to make objective product comparisons.
  • Analytical Skills: Excellent analytical thinking, problem-solving, and evidence-based decision-making abilities.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel: Proficiency with:
    • XLOOKUP and VLOOKUP
    • Pivot Tables
    • Large Datasets
    • Sorting and Filtering
    • Data Validation and Data Cleansing
    • Product Attribute Comparisons
    • Structured Research Templates
  • Research Skills: Ability to independently research medical products using manufacturer documentation, technical specifications, clinical references, and regulatory resources.
  • Technical Documentation: Ability to interpret clinical product specifications, manufacturer Instructions for Use (IFUs), and other technical materials.
  • Data Accuracy: Exceptional attention to detail and ability to identify discrepancies within large product datasets.
  • Critical Thinking: Ability to evaluate incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting information and develop defensible research conclusions.
  • Written Communication: Strong ability to document findings clearly and explain the clinical rationale behind product recommendations.
  • Independent Work: Demonstrated ability to work remotely, manage assigned projects, meet deadlines, and maintain productivity without close supervision.
  • Technology Adaptability: Comfortable learning new research platforms, healthcare databases, and AI-enabled research tools while independently validating findings.
  • Additional Requirements: Strong organizational skills, time management, professionalism, and ability to manage multiple research priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous clinical experience in one or more of the following areas:
    • Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
    • Emergency Department (ED)
    • Medical-Surgical Nursing
    • Progressive Care / Step-Down Units
    • Vascular Access
    • Wound Care
    • Respiratory Therapy
    • General Acute Care or Ambulatory Care
  • Previous experience as a Clinical Product Specialist, Clinical Product Educator, Value Analysis Professional, Healthcare Product Analyst, or Clinical Product Consultant.
  • Experience participating in clinical product evaluations, product conversions, or product standardization initiatives.
  • Previous experience conducting functional equivalency assessments or multi-manufacturer product comparisons.
  • Familiarity with healthcare supply chain operations, sourcing processes, and product selection methodologies.
  • Experience working with ERP systems, healthcare item master data, product master databases, or product information management systems.
  • Understanding of healthcare product packaging hierarchies, units of measure, and product catalog structures.
  • Familiarity with research resources such as:
    • FDA Global Unique Device Identification Database (GUDID)
    • FDA 510(k) Database
    • Manufacturer Specifications and Instructions for Use
    • ECRI
    • Lumere
    • BroadJump
    • Clinical Publications and Peer-Reviewed Research
  • Previous experience developing or maintaining clinical product knowledge databases.
  • Experience working with healthcare supply chain, value analysis, or clinical standardization teams.
  • Strong knowledge of product selection considerations across multiple manufacturers and clinical specialties.
  • Experience managing large-scale, spreadsheet-based research projects requiring high levels of accuracy and documentation.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Clinical Product Research Analyst will be able to:

  • Apply real clinical experience to determine how and why medical products are used in patient care.
  • Identify clinically appropriate product alternatives across competing manufacturers.
  • Evaluate functional equivalency while recognizing important differences that could affect patient care or clinical workflows.
  • Analyze large datasets accurately and efficiently using advanced Excel tools.
  • Research independently through incomplete, conflicting, or unfamiliar product information.
  • Develop evidence-based recommendations supported by reliable documentation and defensible clinical reasoning.
  • Build and maintain accurate product knowledge records that support future research, sourcing, and standardization initiatives.
  • Deliver consistent, high-quality research while meeting deadlines and working independently in a remote environment.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based.

What this opportunity involves

We’re looking for US-based, actively practicing physicians (MD/DO) to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation program. General and internal medicine are our main focus. While each project involves unique tasks, contributors may:

  • Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor “trap” answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
  • Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
  • Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales;
  • Work within three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You’re improving the AI tools you’ll eventually use yourself.

This opportunity is a good fit for US-based physicians open to part-time, non-permanent projects. Ideally, contributors will have:

  • Board certification or completed residency training, with recent direct patient care (attending-level preferred);

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: Washington, Oregon, California, Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, Utah. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for this role:

  • 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue
  • All candidates must be located in one of the following states: Washington, Oregon, California, Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, Utah

An ideal candidate has:

  • Proven track record of consistent quota achievement
  • Experience selling in the midmarket space - medium to large deals sizes
  • Experience with high-volume cold calling
  • Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process
  • SFDC familiarity

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary
$152,000—$190,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

jobs.excerpt: IntellaTriage continues to GROW! IntellaTriage Nurses enjoy the benefits of working from home, providing care, without the stress and expense of commuting each day!
jobs.description:
IntellaTriage continues to GROW!

IntellaTriage Nurses enjoy the benefits of working from home, providing care, without the stress and expense of commuting each day!

**MUST have or be willing to obtain a Compact RN license

**MUST live in/work from a Compact US state

**Minimum of 2 years as a Nurse

**Minimum of 1 year of experience in a fast-paced environment (i.e. ED, Critical Care, Surgical Services, Med/Surg, etc.)

**Must have high speed internet

**Must be tech savvy, enjoy a fast-paced environment, and have no concerns typing

**Must be available to work 2 out of every 3 weekends & 1 weekday per week.

> 3 shifts per 2 week pay period Mon-Fri, rotating 5p-11p CST

> 2 of every 3 weekend rotation (Sat & Sun) rotating 8a-4p/ 2p-10p

Our Nurse Advice Line Nurses:

  • Have proven experience in a fast-paced, critical-thinking environment; ED, Critical Care, Surgical Services, etc.
  • Work a minimum of 2-3 shift per week (Mon-Fri).
  • Preferred scheduling for their weekday requirements.
  • Work 2 weekends or every 3 weeks, both Saturday and Sunday on those weekends with rotating times. (For example: weekend 1: work, weekend 2: work, weekend 3: off)
  • Train for 3 weeks. First week is Monday-Thursday 9a-6p CST. Remaining two weeks training will be dependent upon preceptor availability but will likely be an evening shift.
  • Must have a compact license and live in that compact state. (no states with pending legislation or future implementation dates are considered current compacts)

What is important to know?

We are growing and excited to be able to support our clients’ nursing staffs in the field who need time to focus on work-life balance, as well, while being able to trust that we are there to support them and their patients during nights and weekends!

  • Patient care is #1. We do not have call quotas. We employ the best nurses to provide the best care.
  • When our patients or their families reach our triage line, they immediately speak directly with a nurse.
  • We do not have PRN positions.
  • We are super busy. If you like fast-paced roles, keep reading…
  • Any nurse may pick up additional shifts, if shifts are available for the clients’ they are trained to support.
  • We will provide you with a laptop and headset.
  • Nurses are required to provide their own high-speed internet (only fiberoptic or coaxial cable internet is compatible with our remote call center technology).
  • Our laptop is required to be directly connected to your modem. Working through Wi-Fi is not compatible with our systems. The calls will drop.
  • It is essential to have a home office or quiet space free from noise or distractions in your home (Privacy/HIPAA compliant space is required).
  • Training is provided remotely and is paid; no travel is required in this role.
  • MUST be able to follow instructions (verbal and written) and be comfortable with technology (tech savvy).
  • Must remain in good standing and ensure their home state license remains active.
  • IntellaTriage will cover the cost of non-compact state licensure based on the client(s) that are assigned for support.
  • All nurses must have a compact license and reside/work in that state.
  • Shift prep is a minimum clock-in of 30 minutes prior to taking calls; this is paid time to prepare.
  • Once calls roll to the next team/shift, our nurses remain clocked in and complete any remaining charting before leaving for the day. This may take 30 minutes or this may take 2 hours. It depends on the pace of the calls received during that shift and the pace of your ability to quickly navigate technology and type.

Sound exciting to you?

Then… put those days on the floor and that commute or hours on the road between patients’ homes behind you! Our nurses enjoy working from their own home office; no more purchasing scrubs, expensive takeout, and the large gas bill along with extra wear-and-tear on your vehicle.

Most importantly, working remotely enables you to spend more time with those you love!

Requirements

  • MUST have or be willing to obtain a Compact Nursing License (States with pending legislation or future implementation dates are not considered current compacts until the implementation date.)
  • 3+ years as a RN
  • Experience in a fast-paced environment: i.e. ED, Surgical Services, or Critical Care.
  • Must be comfortable with technology and accessing multiple applications remotely to perform documentation during calls.
  • Ability and comfort typing.
  • Fluency in English is required, additional languages are a bonus.
  • Must physically reside in the U.S. and be legally eligible to work for any employer.
  • Must be able to complete the 3-week orientation and training (Schedule listed in this posting).
  • Must be available to work Saturday & Sunday on your team's required weekends; 2 of every 3 weekends.
  • Holidays as they are required (rotation).
  • Able to handle stress and multitask when calls are coming in (minimum of 5+ calls per hour on weekdays, and much higher on weekends).
  • Able to communicate with patients and families with empathy while also maintaining adherence to client protocols.
  • Must maintain CEU’s as designated by the states you are answering calls in.
  • Must attend any in-services, additional training on an as needed basis.
  • Able to pass background check and nurse licensing check.

Benefits

All Remote Nurse Advice Line RN's, once trained to their originally assigned team are at $25/hourly. All part-time nurses accumulate PTO, based on the number of hours they work (per year). All part-time nurses receive an additional 3-paid-sick-days per year. All part-time nurses are eligible to participate in our 401(k) plan.

jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced, analytical, and highly meticulous Virtual Senior Accounting Support Specialist to manage revenue reporting, Accounts Receivable (AR) tracking, invoicing, and provider payroll support for Perio Providers Group (PPG), a growing periodontal healthcare organization supporting 41 doctors across Southern California.

This is a specialized, high-level accounting support role requiring strong core accounting principles, advanced math skills (including percentage-based calculations), and expert-level Microsoft Excel proficiency (PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, SUMIFS). Operating under established procedures, you will consolidate multi-provider production data, investigate financial discrepancies, and deliver accurate financial summaries without relying on traditional accounting software like QuickBooks.

Working Environment & Core Schedule

  • Role Title: Virtual Senior Accounting Support Specialist
  • Organization: Perio Providers Group (PPG) — Supporting 41 Periodontal Doctors
  • Status: Full-Time (40 Hours / Week)
  • Schedule: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM PST (Pacific Standard Time)
  • Core Technology Stack:Microsoft Excel(Advanced), Outlook, Google Voice, Practice Production Reporting Portals (No QuickBooks access utilized)
  • Primary Scope: Multi-Provider Revenue Consolidation, AR & Invoicing, Production-Based Provider Payroll Audit

Top 3 Daily Tasks

  1. Revenue Management & Month-End Reporting: Collect and consolidate complex daily/monthly production reports across 41 doctors and multiple office locations, auditing figures for discrepancies and maintaining detailed revenue tracking sheets.
  2. Invoicing & Accounts Receivable (AR) Support: Prepare detailed invoice data, review office adjustments, track invoice and payment statuses, flag unusual ledger items, and build comprehensive AR reports in Excel.
  3. Provider Payroll & Production Audit: Audit raw production data underlying provider compensation, maintain payroll tracking spreadsheets, verify percentage-based payout figures against production totals, and prep payroll batches for executive approval.

Core Responsibilities

  • Multi-Location Revenue Consolidation: Extract and aggregate production figures across 41 periodontal providers; audit report entries for accuracy, identify balance discrepancies, and maintain master revenue summary workbooks.
  • Invoicing & Ledger Adjustment Audits: Compile line-item invoice data and supporting documentation; analyze office fee adjustments, refunds, and write-offs, flagging any out-of-policy items for management review.
  • Production-Based Payroll Support: Reconcile doctor production reports against contract compensation structures, calculating complex percentage-based tiers and maintaining structured payroll verification schedules.
  • Advanced Financial Analysis in Excel: Build, maintain, and audit complex financial workbooks using PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, SUMIFS, and custom formulas to support month-end financial closes.
  • Communication & Confidentiality: Maintain secure communication with internal teams via Outlook and Google Voice, following strict data governance, confidentiality, and accounting procedures.

Requirements

  • Accounting & Financial Background: Strong foundational understanding of accounting principles, GAAP standards, invoicing, AR, and financial reporting workflows. (Staff Accountant or Senior Accountant background strongly preferred).
  • Advanced Excel Proficiency: High-level mastery of Microsoft Excel, including hands-on experience building and auditing PivotTables, XLOOKUP / VLOOKUP, and SUMIFS functions. (Candidates without advanced Excel mastery will not be considered).
  • Advanced Mathematical Skills: Demonstrated strength in quantitative analysis, financial auditing, and calculating complex percentage-based compensation or revenue splits.
  • Analytical Discrepancy Auditing: Proven ability to scrutinize large data sets, cross-reference multi-source reports, and spot minor financial discrepancies independently.
  • Procedure Adherence & Independence: Ability to follow established accounting protocols precisely while managing strict monthly close deadlines with high autonomy.
  • Communication & Confidentiality: Excellent written and verbal English communication skills with absolute discretion when handling confidential financial and payroll data.
  • Remote Workspace: Private, quiet, HIPAA/financial-compliant home office equipped with a high-performance computer (PC/Mac), high-speed internet, backup power/internet solutions, and a headset.

Preferred / Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience in Dental, Healthcare, or Medical Group accounting practices.
  • Multi-location or multi-provider financial tracking experience (supporting 20+ providers).
  • Experience auditing production-based or commission-based doctor/provider compensation.

Ideal Candidate Profile

You are a sharp accounting professional who lives in Microsoft Excel. You enjoy diving into complex production data, cross-checking percentage calculations down to the cent, and maintaining bulletproof AR, revenue, and payroll tracking spreadsheets for a multi-provider healthcare group.

jobs.excerpt: Who are we? Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart.
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.

People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.

What is the role?

We are seeking an Assistant Vice President (AVP), Pharmacy who will serve as a strategic pharmacy consultant supporting employer clients in the design, evaluation, and optimization of pharmacy benefit programs. This role will lead pharmacy benefit management (PBM) procurement initiatives, financial and contract analyses, market assessments, vendor evaluations, and client-facing consulting engagements, while overseeing day-to-day operations of the Pharmacy Analytics practice supporting Howden’s middle market teams. The ideal candidate will bring expertise from a PBM, health plan, pharmacy analytics, or pharmacy consulting environment and possess a strong understanding of the evolving pharmacy landscape, including specialty drugs, GLP-1 therapies, PBM pricing models, rebate strategies, financial guarantees, and emerging cost-containment solutions.

What will you be doing?

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to employer clients on pharmacy benefit strategy, plan design, and cost management opportunities.
  • Lead and support PBM market checks, renewals, procurement projects, and formal RFP processes.
  • Oversee day-to-day operations of the Pharmacy Analytics practice for Howden’s middle market teams, including workflow planning, prioritization, resource allocation, and delivery oversight.
  • Manage intake, scoping, and work assignment for PBM RFPs, rebate reconciliations, market checks, contract reviews, and other financial analyses.
  • Analyze PBM financial proposals, pricing guarantees, rebate arrangements, dispensing fees, and contractual terms.
  • Develop, maintain, and oversee claim-level and aggregate financial models used to evaluate PBM proposals, validate pricing guarantees and rebate arrangements, assess pharmacy program performance, and quantify vendor savings opportunities.
  • Establish modeling standards, documented assumptions, quality-control procedures, and peer-review processes to promote accuracy, consistency, transparency, and auditability across pharmacy analytics deliverables.
  • Interpret PBM claims, eligibility, formulary, rebate, specialty, and financial data; identify data-quality issues; and translate analytical findings into clear client recommendations and executive-level deliverables.
  • Provide strategic guidance on specialty pharmacy, biosimilars, GLP-1 medications, cell and gene therapies, and emerging market trends.
  • Review and negotiate pharmacy contract provisions and performance guarantees.
  • Prepare and present client deliverables, executive summaries, and recommendations to employer leadership teams.
  • Support finalist presentations, vendor evaluations, and implementation activities.
  • Collaborate with account teams, producers, and subject matter experts to identify growth opportunities and deliver exceptional client service.
  • Build and maintain relationships with PBMs, specialty pharmacies, clinical vendors, and other strategic partners.

What are we looking for?

Qualifications


  • 7+ years of experience in pharmacy consulting, PBM account management, PBM underwriting, pricing, trade relations, clinical strategy, or related pharmacy benefit roles.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of PBM contracting, rebate programs, pharmacy pricing methodologies, and specialty drug management.
  • Advanced pharmacy financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience building and reviewing claim-level models, evaluating PBM pricing proposals, validating contract guarantees, and working with large pharmacy claims data sets.
  • Exemplary knowledge of pharmacy analytics capabilities, methodologies, coverages, and services, including their application to PBM procurement, market checks, rebate reconciliations, contract reviews, and ongoing financial performance monitoring.
  • Thorough understanding of PBM data layouts, claims and eligibility files, contract structures, financial terms, pricing guarantees, rebate arrangements, and core pharmacy data concepts.
  • Demonstrated ability to oversee analytical workflow, prioritize competing requests, assign work effectively, review outputs, and communicate modeling assumptions, limitations, and results to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to translate complex pharmacy concepts into actionable recommendations for clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Excellent presentation, communication, and relationship management skills.
  • Experience managing multiple projects and client deliverables in a fast-paced environment.
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint; experience with pharmacy analytics and reporting tools is preferred.
  • Ability to travel periodically for client meetings, conferences, and business development opportunities.

Compensation and Benefits

The expected base salary range for this role is $150,000- $190,000; actual base salary will be determined based on factors including candidate experience and work location. This role is classified as exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

In addition to a competitive base salary, employees are eligible to receive a discretionary bonus. Howden also offers a variety of benefits and programs, subject to eligibility, including:


  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including healthcare savings and reimbursement accounts
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Flexible Paid Time Off and paid parental leave
  • Life and Disability insurance

Our sustainability promise

We’re on a life-long journey to become an ever-more sustainable group. It's a commitment to taking care of our people and the world we live in, to doing good business, and to making a positive impact wherever we can. Our governance processes, company policies, and review systems are all geared towards our goal of making a positive impact in the world. You can read more about our sustainability work here.

What do we offer in return?

A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:

  • Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new

  • We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges

  • We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond

Reasonable adjustments

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs. Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.

If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.

*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.
