About Yaqeen Institute

Yaqeen is a nonprofit on a mission to pioneer Islamic research in creative, cutting-edge formats tailored to meet people where they are. We work to dismantle doubts through well-researched truths, nurture conviction by strengthening belief with practical, spiritual guidance, and inspire contribution by reviving our tradition of faithful changemakers, insha’Allah. We’re seeking like-minded professionals who embody Islamic values including sincerity, excellence, and compassion, and want to make a difference in the faith of people worldwide.

Role Description/Overview:

Yaqeen Institute is seeking a technically skilled and creatively ambitious AI & Creative Technology Engineer to help advance how impactful media is imagined, produced, and delivered. Working at the intersection of filmmaking, software engineering, and emerging artificial intelligence, this role will design and build tools that empower our producers, editors, animators, designers, and researchers to create exceptional content with greater efficiency, consistency, and creative possibility.

This role is ideal for a hands-on builder who can move from experimentation to implementation: someone who can prototype AI-assisted visual storytelling, develop custom applications and automations, and integrate new capabilities into everyday production. The right candidate understands that technology should strengthen human creativity, scholarly accuracy, and artistic judgment — never replace them. A strong parallel is the creative technology and production engineering work emerging within leading film studios and AI-native media teams, adapted to Yaqeen's distinctive mission and standards.

What you'll do

Role & Responsibilities:

  • Creative Technology Research & Development: Explore, test, and assess emerging AI tools and creative technologies across video, animation, image, audio, editing, and interactive storytelling. Identify use cases that offer genuine creative or production value.
  • AI-Assisted Visual Production: Develop practical workflows for storyboarding, previsualization, historical environments, animation, motion graphics, visual effects, and other media assets in collaboration with the creative team.
  • Custom Tool & Application Development: Build lightweight internal applications, scripts, plugins, dashboards, and API integrations that address production bottlenecks and make useful AI capabilities accessible to nontechnical teammates.
  • Production Workflow Automation: Improve repetitive tasks such as footage logging, transcription, captioning, media organization, versioning, asset retrieval, localization preparation, and delivery while maintaining human review where needed.
  • Pipeline Design & Integration: Connect AI services and custom tools with established creative software and production systems. Build workflows that are reliable, documented, cost-conscious, and practical for real deadlines.
  • Creative Collaboration & Prototyping: Partner directly with producers, editors, animators, and designers to translate a creative need into a technical solution; iterate on prototypes until they meet the team's artistic and operational standards.
  • Quality, Accuracy & Responsible AI: Establish safeguards for factual reliability, sensitive religious and historical depictions, copyright, privacy, synthetic media, and content provenance. Ensure appropriate editorial and scholarly review before publication.
  • Documentation & Team Enablement: Create clear instructions, reusable templates, and workflow guides; train colleagues to use deployed tools confidently and support their adoption over time.
  • Performance & Continuous Improvement: Evaluate solutions using measurable indicators such as production time saved, cost, output consistency, reliability, and creative quality. Recommend when an AI solution should — or should not — be used.

Qualifications/Required Skills:

  • Proven experience in creative technology, software development, technical artistry, media-pipeline engineering, or workflow automation; a strong portfolio may substitute for a conventional career path.
  • Ability to build and maintain working tools using Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or comparable languages, including integrations with APIs, webhooks, and third-party services.
  • Hands-on experience with generative AI tools and models for at least two of the following: video, images, audio, animation, language, or visual effects; an ability to evaluate limitations as well as strengths.
  • Familiarity with professional media workflows and creative software such as Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, Photoshop, or comparable tools.
  • Comfortable prototyping user-friendly internal applications, managing structured data, troubleshooting technical issues, and working with version control.
  • Strong visual judgment and an appreciation for storytelling, composition, motion, consistency, and production quality.
  • Ability to make prototypes dependable through testing, error handling, documentation, cost awareness, and attention to data security.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, especially when translating technical concepts for creative teammates in a remote environment.
  • A strong passion for Yaqeen's mission and a commitment to editorial integrity, scholarly rigor, and thoughtful use of emerging technology.
  • Experience with node-based AI workflows (e.g., ComfyUI), VFX/3D pipelines, model customization, media asset management, analytics, or cloud deployment is a strong plus.

Application Assignment:

  • Part 1 — Portfolio: Share 2–3 examples of tools, automations, creative AI workflows, or production-facing projects you have built. Briefly describe the problem, your contribution, and the outcome for each example. Links, short screen recordings, or case studies are welcome.
  • Part 2 — Yaqeen Workflow Proposal: Select an existing Yaqeen video or series and identify one specific opportunity where AI or creative technology could meaningfully improve storytelling, production quality, or team efficiency.

In 1–2 pages, explain the existing challenge, the solution you would build, the tools or technical approach you would use, how you would protect quality and accuracy, and how you would measure success.

A simple diagram or mockup is welcome; a working prototype is optional, not required. Do not use confidential materials or paid subscriptions for this exercise.

Yaqeen Institute embraces a philosophy that values and promotes diversity. Our goal is to attract, develop, retain, and advance a talented and diverse workforce within a culture where all employees are empowered to reach their fullest potential.

Please note that all career opportunities at Yaqeen Institute are subject to a three-month probationary period, during which we assess performance, alignment with our values, and mutual fit to ensure long-term success in the role.

Everything we build helps the salon and medspa industry thrive.

We're also a Certified B Corp, and 25% of the company is owned by Phoresters. When the company grows, everyone has a stake in that.

The Opportunity

We are inviting Associate Software Engineers to join our 2027 Graduate Programme, ready to build their skills, learn from experienced teammates and begin contributing to building great features our customers love.

You'll join a Product & Engineering community that cares about the businesses we serve, the quality of our work and each other. You'll learn how software is developed in a team, from understanding a problem and writing code to testing solutions and improving them through feedback.

You won't be expected to know everything from day one. You'll start with well-scoped tasks, supported by experienced engineers, and build towards more complex work as your skills and confidence develop.

What you'll get to do

  • Build your engineering foundations: Develop your coding, debugging, testing and version-control skills through practical, hands-on work.

  • Contribute to real products: Work on bug fixes and small enhancements that help improve the software our customers rely on.

  • Understand our customers: Build a strong understanding of the hair, beauty and medspa businesses we serve and the challenges they face.

  • Learn with AI: Use AI tools as a core part of our engineering workflow to support your learning, build your skills and develop your judgement.

  • Learn from experienced engineers: Take part in pair programming, code reviews and coaching, asking questions and putting feedback into practice.

  • Discover how software gets delivered: Join team planning, daily check-ins and retrospectives as you learn how teams collaborate, solve problems and deliver improvements.

  • Develop good engineering habits: Practise writing clean, maintainable code, testing your work and documenting your solutions in line with team conventions.

  • Grow your independence: Take ownership of your tasks, learn from mistakes and gradually take on more responsibility as your skills develop.

To be eligible, you'll need:

  • Third-level education in a related field, or a relevant certification supported by strong evidence of personal projects.

  • To have completed your qualification within the last two years, with no more than two years' experience in a related role.

More about you

You don't need to arrive as a fully independent engineer. We're looking for a solid foundation, curiosity and a genuine enthusiasm for learning.

You'll bring:

  • Familiarity with at least one programming language, such as Java, Kotlin or JavaScript.

  • An understanding of programming fundamentals and object-oriented design.

  • An awareness of concepts such as REST APIs and relational databases.

  • Some experience of coding, testing or collaborative development through your studies, personal projects, an internship or another learning experience.

  • Curiosity, a willingness to ask questions and an openness to feedback.

  • Clear communication, a collaborative approach and an interest in the people who use what you build.

  • A sense of ownership over your learning and assigned tasks, with the flexibility to adapt as you develop.

We're interested in what you've learned so far, how you approach problems and what you're excited to learn next.

Room to grow, support to get there

At Phorest, we’re passionate about growing our own timber. We know every career has its own path, and we’re here to help you along yours. Through hands-on guidance, pair programming, code reviews and coaching, you’ll build confidence step by step, moving from well-defined tasks towards greater independence.

Across Phorest, we also offer dedicated Learning Days, a mentoring programme, career coaching, development programmes and learning tools to help you shape your career.

Our aim is to help you build the technical skills, collaborative habits and confidence to grow into an effective software engineer.

Benefits

🧘 Your wellbeing is important to us - we provide private healthcare, 2 Wellness Days, an employee assistance program and a free online GP service.

💰 As part of our Financial Wellbeing, we provide competitive Compensation, an Employee Share Purchase Scheme, Pension, Life Assurance, and Income Protection.

🚵🏿 We help you travel by providing a bike to work scheme as well as tax saver transport tickets.

🦸‍♀️ We support the women who work in Phorest by offering 2 weeks leave for Fertility Treatment, Pregnancy Loss and Menopause.

🍼 We care for your family and provide Enhanced Maternity and Paternity Benefits.

🌳 We grow our own timber! We provide a great learning environment and extensive development opportunities. We run development programs and provide access to many online resources including LinkedIn learning.

🏠 Moving house? Phorest employees get 3 moving days.

Want to learn more about Phorest? Check out for our blog and Insights on building an evergreen company from the team here at Phorest.

Phorest is an equal opportunity employer. For this position, flexi-time and working from home is possible. We are also open to remote work. Get in touch to ask for more information or to chat about your future with Phorest!

Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalised folks tend to only apply when they check every box. So if you think you have what it takes, but don't necessarily meet every single point on the job description, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit.

Description of Duties

We’re looking for a Staff Technical Writer to create documentation and learning content that helps people adopt and master Grafana’s observability products. You’ll work with engineers, product managers, and the Grafana writing team to produce content for a range of products and audiences, from first-time users to experienced practitioners.   • Mentor teammates and share practices that raise the quality of the team’s work.

Requirements

  • Ownership. You manage multiple projects and work well both independently and collaboratively.

  • Bonus: Experience with observability, monitoring, or cloud-native tooling, or contributing to open source documentation.

Company Overview
Our client builds technology that helps families access public benefits. It also helps governments, health plans and other organizations run those programs more effectively. Their work with state and federal agencies, Medicaid organizations and health plans is growing fast. As it does, trust, security, privacy and compliance have become core product requirements.

Your Role

This is not a typical PM role where compliance is just one feature area. It's also not a policy-only compliance job, and not a pure security engineering seat. We're looking for a trust and compliance expert who is also an excellent product leader. You'll own the strategy and requirements for the company's Trust layer: the platform features that make security, privacy, compliance and auditability part of how the software works. You'll also run the trust and compliance program day to day, and own a company-wide trust transformation. This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role. You'll understand a requirement, work out what it means for the business and the software, bring the right people together, and see the work through.

You’ll:

  • Lead the Trust Transformation

    • Own the company's new trust operating model across Product, Engineering, Customer Delivery and company operations.

    • Turn regulatory, customer, security and privacy requirements into clear product, technical and operational requirements.

    • Partner with the Trust engineering lead to design and build the Trust layer.

    • Set durable approaches to production access, data handling, environment separation, release governance and evidence collection.

  • Build Trust Into the Product

    • Own product direction for:

      • identity and access management, with least-privilege access

      • tenant and environment isolation

      • data classification, privacy, consent and data provenance

      • audit logging and change history

      • retention and data governance

      • secure release and deployment controls

      • continuous control monitoring

    • Move controls out of manual processes and into reusable, software-enforced capabilities, so the compliant path becomes the default path.

  • Own the Trust & Compliance Program

    • Maintain policies, controls and evidence in Vanta, and coordinate control owners across the company.

    • Own the compliance roadmap and turn new requirements into cross-functional initiatives people can execute.

    • Keep a clear view of risks, control gaps, exceptions and remediation commitments.

    • Give leadership clear recommendations when trust requirements force business or product trade-offs.

  • Lead Audits, Assurance & Security Programs

    • Keep the company continuously ready for recurring SOC 2 audits.

    • Coordinate external audits, penetration tests and vendor risk reviews, and drive findings through to closure.

    • Launch the NIST 800-series alignment program and help chart the path toward FedRAMP-aligned practices.

  • Be the External Trust Lead

    • Act as the main contact for customer security, privacy, compliance and AI-governance requirements.

    • Lead responses to security questionnaires, privacy and AI-use assessments, and procurement reviews.

    • Represent the company with security, legal and procurement teams at government agencies, Medicaid organizations and health plans.

You Bring:

  • Experience in regulated environments such as government, public-sector tech, healthcare, Medicaid, health plans or similar high-trust industries.

  • Working knowledge of SOC 2, NIST 800-series controls, HIPAA and government security standards.

  • A track record of leading audits, security questionnaires, penetration-testing programs and remediation.

  • Strong product management skills: problem definition, requirements, prioritization, roadmap ownership and cross-functional delivery.

  • Enough technical fluency to go deep with senior engineers on architecture, access models, data flows and controls.

  • The credibility and communication skills to stand in front of sophisticated customer security teams.

  • Comfort working autonomously while the function and the product are both still being built.

  • You must be based in the U.S.

What’s Offered

  • A fully remote role within the U.S.

  • Competitive compensation based on experience.

  • Real ownership: you'll shape how trust is built into both the platform and the way the company operates.

  • A team that may grow around you as the function scales.

  • Possess excellent written and verbal communication skills with patients, colleagues, and cross-functional partners

  • Hold a current Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration and federal DEA registration
  • Have experience in a rapidly scaling healthcare or digital health organization

nesto is Canada’s leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go — with total transparency and no haggling.

Nesto Group

Nesto Group is Canada's leading provider of mortgage technology and financing solutions, with more than CAD $80 billion in residential and commercial mortgages under administration. Trusted by many of the country's leading financial institutions, we combine over 50 years of mortgage expertise with proprietary cloud and AI technology to transform the future of lending.

Powered by our proprietary cloud and AI technology, nesto has become one of Canada's fastest-growing mortgage lenders, gaining market share across direct-to-consumer (D2C) residential lending, the broker channel, and multi-family commercial lending. Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer-focused solutions.

Operating through our family of brands—CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud—our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services. Learn more at:

Life at nesto

At nesto, we're passionate about challenging the status quo and building a better mortgage experience and saving money on their mortgages for Canadians. We foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, and creativity where every team member is empowered to take ownership, make an impact, and grow. If you're looking to solve meaningful problems alongside ambitious, supportive teammates, you'll feel right at home here.

About the role

At nesto, we are building Maestro: an AI platform that makes mortgage professionals dramatically more productive across sales, underwriting, and loan servicing. This is not "AI theater"— Maestro is already live, actively assisting underwriters with real files today.

As the Product Manager for the AI Platform, you will help turn this early proof-of-concept into the platform that defines AI-augmented lending in Canada. You will sit at the intersection of complex operational workflows, machine learning, and real mortgage expertise to turn hard problems into shipped product.

Why nesto’s approach to AI is different:

  • We sit where the work happens: We have direct access to the workflows, policies, and expert feedback inside real mortgage operations across the full lending journey.
  • Built for a regulated industry: Most AI companies build isolated demos or point solutions. We embed AI directly into production, continuously learning from human underwriter judgment.
  • End-to-end integration: We don't just solve one piece of the puzzle; we connect the full lending stack to make AI practically and systemically useful.

What you'll be doing here

  • Turn complex operational reality into clear PRDs, decision logic, and shipped product
  • Work closely with ML, engineering, underwriting ops, and business stakeholders to define and deliver the roadmap
  • Define and improve the metrics that matter: throughput, time-to-decision, accuracy, and capacity gained
  • Build tight feedback loops between AI output and expert human judgment
  • Keep execution moving in a high-ambiguity, high-accountability environment
  • Stay ahead of how AI is reshaping mortgage origination and bring informed recommendations to the roadmap
  • Share what you discover — how you work should make the people around you better

Who we're looking for

The profile.

  • 3-5 years of experience in consulting or a high-ownership product role in a complex environment
  • Ability to write clearly, think structurally, and go deep on systems, data, and edge cases
  • Comfortable operating without perfect inputs — you find the truth, make the call, and drive the work forward
  • Proven, active fluency with AI tools across your PM workflow: discovery, testing, documentation, analysis, and measurement.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex concepts clearly to non-experts in Product and Engineering

Preferred but not a must

  • Mortgage or regulated financial services experience — curiosity, rigor, and execution matter more
  • Familiarity with LOS systems, origination platforms, or lending technology
  • Exposure to AI or ML-assisted decisioning, document intelligence, or automation in a financial services context
  • Familiarity with broker and advisor-facing workflows and the nuances of supported versus self-serve client journeys

  • Final Stakeholder Interview – 45 minutes
  • Criminal Record and Reference Checks + Offer

CloudM is an award-winning SaaS platform headquartered in Manchester, with offices in London and Varna (Bulgaria), and customers in 107 countries. We help over 50,000 organisations including LinkedIn, Uber, Netflix,, and Spotify, get the most out of Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, through three core products: Migrate, Automate, and Continuity.

From IT admin and onboarding to archiving and migrations, CloudM takes the complexity out of SaaS data management so our customers can focus on what matters. Backed by Marlin Equity Partners, we've grown from humble Manchester beginnings into a global business with a team of over 70 brilliant people across the UK and Europe.

If you share our ambition, we'd love you to be part of it!

Role Overview:

This is a senior, hands on role owning the systems that run CloudM’s revenue operating model. Salesforce sits at the centre of it and you will be accountable for it. You will inherit a platform that has grown quickly alongside the business, so your job is to stabilise it, document it, rationalise the automation that has accumulated, and run it as a dependable foundation for Sales, Marketing, Customer Success and Finance as we scale.

Broadly, the shape of the role is:

  • Salesforce platform ownership, remediation and day to day support: around 85%

  • DealHub quoting administration: around 10%

  • HubSpot maintenance and support: under 5%

You will be the only internal Salesforce specialist, with an external Salesforce partner available for deep technical work. That means you need the judgement to know what to build yourself, what to hand out, and how to hold a supplier to a standard.

This role suits someone who enjoys improving systems, asks clarifying questions before building, and is as comfortable explaining a report to a sales manager as they are rebuilding a broken flow.

Responsibilities:

  • Salesforce platform ownership: Full administrative ownership of the Salesforce org. Users, permission sets, profiles and roles, objects, fields, record types, page layouts, validation rules, flows and routine maintenance, managed through sandbox with proper testing before release.

  • Automation remediation: Assess the automation that exists today, rationalise it, and rebuild what is not fit for purpose. Declarative by default, code only where genuinely warranted, everything documented and supportable by someone other than you.

  • Support and request management: Act as first line support for the revenue teams. Triage and prioritise the request queue, resolve to agreed timescales, and fix the cause behind repeat requests rather than the symptom.

  • Quoting and deal desk: Administer DealHub so quote templates, playbooks, the product and pricing catalogue and approval workflows reflect our commercial guardrails. Maintain the DealHub to Salesforce mapping and support the sales team through quote build issues.

  • Data quality and reporting: Regular audits, de duplication and health checks, plus reports and dashboards covering pipeline, funnel conversion, renewals and forecasting inputs. Understand the question behind the request and offer a view, not just the numbers.

  • Integrations: Maintain the Salesforce to HubSpot sync and support Marketing’s use of the platform.

  • External delivery: Own the relationship with our external Salesforce partner. Write clear requirements, challenge proposed designs, test and accept delivered work, and make sure it is documented and maintainable in house.

  • Documentation and enablement: Keep system and process documentation current, produce simple guides, run drop in sessions, and promote good data habits across the business.

In your first six months we would expect the org properly documented, a prioritised remediation plan agreed with the highest risk items delivered, the support queue running to a predictable and visible standard, and DealHub quoting configuration aligned to current commercial guardrails.

Key Skills

  • Comfortable owning a live support queue and making prioritisation calls under pressure

  • Confidence building reports and dashboards, with the ability to ask clarifying questions, understand the use case, and provide insights rather than just numbers

jobs.description:
Company Overview
Our client is a remote, cloud-based accounting firm offering bookkeeping, tax and fractional CFO services to owner-operated businesses nationwide, including short-term rentals, campgrounds and hotels. Founded in 2022 by a serial founder, the firm now also covers tax planning, equity management and data engineering. It’s building an AI engine that prepares returns, so licensed CPAs spend their time on judgment, not data entry.

Your Role

This is not a “review returns against someone else’s checklist” role. The firm’s AI engine already prepares 1040, 1065, 1120S and C corp returns, and each needs a licensed CPA’s signature before it reaches the IRS. You’re that signature, and the person who decides what it takes to earn it. The review workflow is still being set up, so the rules for catching the engine’s mistakes are yours to write: K-1s, basis tracking and multi-state returns. You work directly with the founder and the engineers. When the engine gets something wrong, you’re talking to the people who can fix it. Success looks like this: the errors you log early stop appearing, other reviewers work from your playbook, and review time per return drops without accuracy slipping.

You’ll:

  • Return sign-off

    • Review AI-prepared 1040, 1065, 1120S and C corp returns, and decide under your own license whether each is signed, sent back or held

    • Focus where software tends to slip: K-1 pass-throughs, basis tracking and multi-state allocations

    • Trace figures back to the source documents the engine read

  • Review rules and QA

    • With the founder and engineers, define the edge-case rules, AI error checks and QA steps around the engine

    • Write each rule in plain steps and mark it as a hard stop or a judgment call

    • Decide which returns get a light pass and which need a full read

  • Feedback to product

    • Log each engine error by form, line and cause, with an example an engineer can reproduce

    • Help work out whether a wrong number came from document scanning, a prompt or the schedule logic, then test the fix alongside engineering

  • Compliance and tax strategy

Position Overview

The Department Chair position supports Calbright College’s mission to offer competency-based, workforce-relevant programs for adult learners through high-impact andragogical practices in online, skills-based curriculum and assessment. In collaboration with the Dean of Learning and Instruction, the Department Chair ensures program quality, workforce relevancy, and continuous improvement of the Health Science Programs.

The Department Chair provides leadership for Health Science program planning, implementation, workforce alignment, and continuous improvement. The Chair works collaboratively with faculty, industry partners, accrediting agencies, and healthcare organizations to ensure programs meet workforce demands, regulatory requirements, and industry standards. The position supports program development, approval processes, the identification of experiential learning opportunities, healthcare partnerships, and advisory council engagement to ensure graduates are prepared for employment in high-demand healthcare fields.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities

The duties below are representative of the role and are not intended to cover all of the
duties performed within the scope of work.

  • Collaborate with Learning and Instruction leadership to support program approval
    processes, including state, accreditation, certification, and regulatory requirements applicable to Health Science programs.
  • Monitor healthcare industry trends, workforce demands, certification requirements, and regulatory changes to ensure the program's ongoing relevance and compliance.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Health Science programs utilizing competency-based and skills-based learning models.
  • Leads regular program-level meetings to review program quality, continuous improvement, and student success metrics and data.
  • Works with cross-functional teams (including program faculty and staff) to ensure program outcomes, assessment measures, and course content are rigorous, responsive, and relevant to workforce skills and needs. Support Adjunct Faculty in setting annual SMART goals to support student success.
  • Oversee adjunct faculty in the assigned department area, including performing quarterly and annual reviews, approving timesheets, training, mentorship, referring student cases, and assisting with escalations. Reviews and monitors student and course feedback to ensure the student voice is represented, and provides recommendations for content and program improvements.
  • Lead the program review process by overseeing review cycles, collecting and analyzing data, engaging stakeholders for input, and preparing comprehensive reports to support continuous improvement and informed decision-making.
  • Leads with a data-informed mindset to validate quality, analyze student outcomes data, and contribute to trend analysis and metric tracking across programs.
  • Support the identification, evaluation, development, and maintenance of clinical, practicum, internship, apprenticeship, and other experiential learning opportunities aligned with program outcomes and accreditation requirements.
  • Collaborate with external partners to ensure experiential learning environments provide appropriate opportunities for student skill development and workforce readiness.
  • Lead Health Science Advisory Councils and engage healthcare employers, licensing bodies, workforce agencies, and industry experts to ensure program alignment with workforce needs, credentialing requirements, emerging healthcare trends, and industry-recognized certifications.
  • Develop and maintain partnerships with healthcare organizations, employers, professional associations, and workforce agencies to support student success and workforce alignment.
  • Maintain relevance in the discipline, including but not limited to certifications, professional development, and networking.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned that support the objective of the position.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • In-depth knowledge in one or more department program areas.
  • Knowledge of and commitment to competency-based education and assessment forward design.
  • Knowledge of healthcare workforce trends, healthcare delivery systems, regulatory requirements, and industry-recognized credentials.
  • Knowledge of healthcare program accreditation, certification, and approval processes.
  • Ability to develop and maintain productive partnerships with healthcare organizations, employers, workforce boards, and professional associations.
  • Knowledge of experiential learning, clinical education, internship, practicum, and work-based learning models.
  • Ability to interpret labor market information and workforce data to support program development and continuous improvement.
  • Knowledge of program review processes, outcomes assessment, and key performance metrics.
  • Working knowledge of program development/design and performance metrics
  • Collaboration and the ability to work across teams toward a unified goal.
  • Effective communicator and resolution-oriented towards students if/as appropriate within the program(s).
  • Effectively communicates and collaborates with fellow faculty members within
    and across disciplines and programs.
  • An innovative and student-centric thought leader in discipline and industry practice.
  • Capable of leading and promoting change management.
  • Demonstrate understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, staff, and faculty.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Baccalaureate degree in Nursing, Allied Health, Health Sciences, Public Health, Healthcare Administration, or a related health discipline.
  • Minimum three years of professional experience in healthcare, health sciences education, workforce development, healthcare administration, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting program quality, curriculum development, workforce alignment, regulatory compliance, or student success initiatives.

Desired Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Nursing, Health Sciences, Public Health, Healthcare Administration, Healthcare Education, or a related discipline.
  • Current professional licensure or certification in an applicable healthcare field.
  • Experience with healthcare accreditation, certification, or board approval
    processes.
  • Experience developing partnerships with healthcare employers, clinical organizations, workforce agencies, or industry stakeholders.
  • Experience with competency-based education, skills-based learning, or
    workforce-focused educational models.
  • Online teaching, online program administration, or adult learning experience.
  • Experience leading advisory councils, workforce advisory boards, or employer
    engagement initiatives.

Working Conditions and Travel

  • Calbright College is a statewide online college where all instruction and support are done via various online technologies both in person and remotely. Calbright College has administrative offices in Sacramento available for use. When working remotely, employees should be able and willing to use the digital communication tools used by the college and to work on a computer for extended periods. Although this is a primarily remote position, there may be instances in which you will be required to attend meetings or travel to in-person sites (clinical affiliates).
  • Regular attendance is considered an essential job function; the inability to meet attendance requirements may preclude the employee from retaining employment.
  • The person holding this position is considered a mandated reporter under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with
    the requirements set forth in Calbright College policies, procedures, and Title IX.
  • Calbright College celebrates all forms of diversity and is deeply committed to fostering an inclusive environment within which students, staff, administrators, and faculty thrive. Individuals interested in advancing Calbright College’s strategic diversity goals are strongly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodations will be provided for qualified applicants with disabilities who self-disclose.
  • Requires the ability to function in a remote online instructional environment, performing work of primarily a sedentary nature. Requires the ability to use hearing and speech to make presentations to groups and carry on conversations over the phone and in-person. Requires speaking skills to communicate with staff and students in one-on-one and small group settings, on the phone, and to distinguish sound prompts from various types of equipment. Requires near visual acuity to read printed materials and computer screens. Requires sufficient hand/arm/finger dexterity to retrieve work materials, operate a personal computer keyboard, and operate standard office equipment. Requires the ability to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
  • Work is performed indoors where minimal safety considerations exist.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Calbright College provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Calbright College complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

Who We Are

Calbright College is one of California’s newest community colleges – the first statewide, online campus designed to bridge the gap between employers with unfilled positions and students who don’t have either the time or money to attend a traditional school. Our mission is to increase economic mobility and close equity gaps for working adults who lack easy access to traditional forms of higher education by offering online, flexible, affordable skills-based programs that provide tangible economic value for both working adults and hiring managers.

nesto is Canada’s leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go — with total transparency and no haggling.

Fast, simple, and fully digital, nesto has been recognized as CLA Lender of the Year for three consecutive years. That's the bright side of mortgages.

Nesto Group

Nesto Group is Canada's leading provider of mortgage technology and financing solutions, with more than CAD $80 billion in residential and commercial mortgages under administration. Trusted by many of the country's leading financial institutions, we combine over 50 years of mortgage expertise with proprietary cloud and AI technology to transform the future of lending.

Powered by our proprietary cloud and AI technology, nesto has become one of Canada's fastest-growing mortgage lenders, gaining market share across direct-to-consumer (D2C) residential lending, the broker channel, and multi-family commercial lending. Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer-focused solutions.

Operating through our family of brands—CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud—our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services. Learn more at:

Life at nesto

At nesto, we're passionate about challenging the status quo and building a better mortgage experience and saving money on their mortgages for Canadians. We foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, and creativity where every team member is empowered to take ownership, make an impact, and grow. If you're looking to solve meaningful problems alongside ambitious, supportive teammates, you'll feel right at home here.

About the role

At nesto, we are building Maestro: an AI platform that makes mortgage professionals dramatically more productive across sales, underwriting, and loan servicing. This is not "AI theater"— Maestro is already live, actively assisting underwriters with real files today.

As the Product Manager for the AI Platform, you will help turn this early proof-of-concept into the platform that defines AI-augmented lending in Canada. You will sit at the intersection of complex operational workflows, machine learning, and real mortgage expertise to turn hard problems into shipped product.

Why nesto’s approach to AI is different:

  • We sit where the work happens: We have direct access to the workflows, policies, and expert feedback inside real mortgage operations across the full lending journey.
  • Built for a regulated industry: Most AI companies build isolated demos or point solutions. We embed AI directly into production, continuously learning from human underwriter judgment.
  • End-to-end integration: We don't just solve one piece of the puzzle; we connect the full lending stack to make AI practically and systemically useful.

What you'll be doing here

  • Turn complex operational reality into clear PRDs, decision logic, and shipped product
  • Work closely with ML, engineering, underwriting ops, and business stakeholders to define and deliver the roadmap
  • Define and improve the metrics that matter: throughput, time-to-decision, accuracy, and capacity gained
  • Build tight feedback loops between AI output and expert human judgment
  • Keep execution moving in a high-ambiguity, high-accountability environment
  • Stay ahead of how AI is reshaping mortgage origination and bring informed recommendations to the roadmap
  • Share what you discover — how you work should make the people around you better

Who we're looking for

The profile.

  • 3-5 years of experience in consulting or a high-ownership product role in a complex environment
  • Ability to write clearly, think structurally, and go deep on systems, data, and edge cases
  • Comfortable operating without perfect inputs — you find the truth, make the call, and drive the work forward
  • Proven, active fluency with AI tools across your PM workflow: discovery, testing, documentation, analysis, and measurement.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex concepts clearly to non-experts in Product and Engineering

Preferred but not a must

  • Mortgage or regulated financial services experience — curiosity, rigor, and execution matter more
  • Familiarity with LOS systems, origination platforms, or lending technology
  • Exposure to AI or ML-assisted decisioning, document intelligence, or automation in a financial services context
  • Familiarity with broker and advisor-facing workflows and the nuances of supported versus self-serve client journeys

Interview process

How we get to know each other.

  • Recruiter Screen – 30 minutes
  • Discovery Call with Director of Product – 30 minutes
  • Take-home Assignment followed by Presentation and Q&A – 60 minutes
  • Final Stakeholder Interview – 45 minutes
  • Criminal Record and Reference Checks + Offer

Why You'll Love Working Here

We believe great people do their best work when they're supported professionally, personally, and financially. That's why we offer a comprehensive rewards package designed to help you thrive at every stage of your career.

  • Competitive Rewards — Competitive compensation, performance incentives (where applicable), and recognition for your contributions.
  • Health & Wellness — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, Health & Wellness Spending Accounts (where applicable), telemedicine, Employee Assistance Programs, and mental health support for you and your family.
  • Time to Recharge — Generous vacation (4 weeks), floater days, and statutory holidays to help you recharge.
  • Planning for the Future — RRSP matching to support your long-term financial wellbeing.
  • Family Support — Enhanced maternity and parental leave top-up programs.
  • Learning & Growth — Education assistance, mentorship, training, and opportunities to build your career across Nesto Group.
  • Tools for Success — Modern technology, collaborative teams, and the resources you need to do your best work.


Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At Nesto Group, we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to succeed.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis), persons with disabilities, members of racialized communities, women, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

If you require accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process, we are committed to working with you to meet your needs.

Position Location: Remote - work virtually from anywhere in the United States

Salary

QC Servion recognizes salary ranges from job boards do not necessarily reflect our pay ranges. In many instances we out-compete those ranges for well-qualified candidates.

Job Summary

We're looking for a Program Manager to drive day-to-day execution of large-scale data center programs across the QC Ecosystem. This is the role that keeps everything moving — coordinating across ecosystem entities, partners, vendors, and stakeholders to ensure commitments are executed, milestones are achieved, and issues are resolved before they impact delivery.

This role sits at the intersection of program planning, execution, and coordination. In addition to overseeing active program delivery, the Program Manager helps coordinate new opportunities as they move from proposal and planning through mobilization and kickoff, ensuring key stakeholders are engaged, execution plans are aligned, and critical milestones remain on track.

Essential Functions

Program Execution & Delivery

  • Drive day-to-day execution against master program schedules and phase-gate milestones.
  • Coordinate activities across ecosystem entities, consultants, contractors, vendors, and client stakeholders.
  • Serve as the primary coordination point between the PMO and teams executing work in the field.
  • Facilitate working sessions that keep projects aligned, risks visible, and decisions moving forward.
  • Monitor program performance and proactively identify potential impacts to schedule, scope, and delivery.
  • Maintain accountability for action items, commitments, and program deliverables.

Program Mobilization & Kickoff Coordination

  • Support the transition of new opportunities from proposal development through program kickoff.
  • Coordinate across QC Ecosystem entities to align scope, deliverables, staffing plans, schedules, and execution assumptions.
  • Track pre-award, mobilization, and startup milestones to ensure readiness for execution.
  • Identify gaps, risks, and dependencies during planning and mobilization activities.
  • Facilitate kickoff planning and ensure successful handoff from business development and proposal teams to delivery teams.
  • Help establish governance structures, communication plans, reporting cadence, and stakeholder alignment before execution begins.

Schedule, Risk & Issue Management

  • Maintain the working program schedule and identify slippage before it becomes a delivery issue.
  • Monitor risks, issues, dependencies, and constraints across multiple workstreams.
  • Drive issue resolution by assigning ownership, establishing timelines, and following through to completion.
  • Escalate risks and challenges to program leadership when appropriate.
  • Support phase-gate reviews and readiness assessments.

Cross-Entity Coordination

  • Coordinate activities across multiple QC Ecosystem entities and external partners.
  • Facilitate collaboration between technical, operational, commercial, and delivery teams.
  • Ensure stakeholders remain aligned on priorities, timelines, and responsibilities.
  • Support communication between leadership teams, project teams, and field personnel.

Program Reporting & Governance

  • Own execution-focused program reporting and status updates.
  • Partner with Project Controls and Business Analysts to ensure accurate reporting and visibility.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly program updates for stakeholders and leadership.
  • Maintain program documentation, action logs, risk registers, and decision tracking.
  • Support governance reviews and executive reporting requirements.

What Success Looks Like

  • Program milestones are achieved and phase-gate requirements are completed successfully.
  • New opportunities transition smoothly from proposal through mobilization and kickoff.
  • Scope, staffing plans, schedules, and execution expectations are aligned before delivery begins.
  • Risks, issues, and dependencies are identified and addressed before impacting program execution.

Position Overview:

Rainey Property Management is seeking an experienced Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist to support a portfolio of affordable housing communities across Texas and Florida. This position plays a critical role in ensuring compliance with HUD Section 8, Project-Based Section 8 (PBRA/PBV), and Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program requirements.

This is a specialized affordable housing compliance position. Candidates must have direct, hands-on experience administering HUD and/or LIHTC affordable housing programs. Experience in corporate, healthcare, banking, IT, cybersecurity, legal, regulatory, or other non-housing compliance fields does not meet the requirements of this role.

The ideal candidate has strong knowledge of affordable housing regulations, experience supporting audits and management reviews, and the ability to provide guidance and training to onsite teams.

  • Review and approve:

    • Verifications of income and assets
    • Rent calculations, HAP rents, and utility allowances
  • Monitor adherence to:
    • HUD Handbook 4350.3 and related guidance
    • IRS Section 42 requirements

  • Maintain accurate, audit-ready documentation in property management and compliance systems

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience with:
    • HUD Section 8
    • Project-Based Section 8 (PBRA and/or PBV)
    • LIHTC compliance
  • Working knowledge of:
    • HUD Handbook 4350.3
    • IRS Section 42 regulations
    • TDHCA and FHFC compliance monitoring requirements
  • Experience supporting MORs and state agency audits
  • Ability to independently review tenant files and income calculations
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and time-management skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook)

Preferred Qualifications

  • BOS, TCS, COS, or similar affordable housing certifications
  • Experience with mixed-finance properties (LIHTC + HUD layered financing)
  • Familiarity with compliance and property management software (ResMan, Yardi, OneSite, etc.)
  • Experience working with multi-state portfolios
  • Ability to travel periodically within Texas and Florida, as needed

What We Offer

  • Supportive, compliance-focused culture

Job Type:  Full-Time | Location:Dallas/Fort Worth, Texas  | Department: Engineering | Reporting to: Global Director, Asset Management and Operational Excellence | Work Location Type:  #remote

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

Reporting to the Global Director, Asset Management & Operational Excellence, the Associate Director, Data Center Infrastructure Readiness & Performance is accountable for taking IREN’s data centre infrastructure and facilities from construction and commissioning into operations, and for the operating standards and performance governance that keep them reliable through their operating life. The role is the liaison from design engineering and construction through commissioning into Operations: it brings Operations along through the L1 to L5 commissioning stages and accepts each stage on behalf of Operations. It sets the operating parameters, guardrails and risk-based limits that protect asset health and reliability, and owns the performance frameworks, KPIs and governance processes that let the fleet scale while maintaining reliability. The role leads the Operational Excellence & Compliance pillar, growing from a team of one to a multi-site team of Operational Readiness & Compliance Leads as the portfolio expands. It is grounded in facility engineering and 24/7 critical-facilities operations: electrical and mechanical infrastructure, commissioning, maintenance and operating discipline.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

Responsibilities

  • Own operational readiness for the transition from construction and commissioning into live operations: set the readiness protocol (Level 1 to Level 5), accept handover from the construction and commissioning organization on behalf of Operations and hold the acceptance gate at each level, and lead the Operational Readiness & Compliance Leads deployed to each new site through ramp-up and stabilization.
  • Set the operating parameters, guardrails and risk-based limits that protect asset health, and lead the business case for bringing select maintenance and operational functions in-house where it improves cost or reliability.
  • Own the performance framework, KPIs and stewardship process, including dashboards for maintenance completion, work order resolution and labour efficiency, that give leadership visibility and drive decisions as the portfolio scales; own the reporting partnership with the integrated operations centre and the data model the KPIs read from.
  • Own the operating standards suite (SOPs, MOPs, EOPs, maintenance playbooks and technical documentation) across IREN’s data centre portfolio, setting the standard method for maintenance effectiveness, work execution and operational planning and assuring it is followed.
  • Lead the operational audit and assurance program: set the audit framework, direct reviews of site adherence to company and customer requirements, and hold sites to corrective action closure.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives affecting site readiness, scalability and operational performance, and shape the operating model, systems and practices that support growth.
  • Define the competencies required to operate and maintain assets to IREN’s operating standards; support Operations and HSSE in building the training and exercise programs against them.
  • Hold technical authority for the operating standards, readiness protocol and operational management of change: approve standards and deviations within them, reduce approval timelines while strengthening audit and compliance readiness, and escalate enterprise-level deviations to the Global Director.
  • Own the lessons-learned system and the operational governance framework for the portfolio, institutionalizing consistency and repeatability globally.
  • Act as the senior interface between site operations, the commissioning organization and corporate operational excellence, accountable for organizational readiness across the business and serving as the commissioning-to-operations liaison.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline (Engineering, Technical Studies, or equivalent), with relevant certifications or technical leadership training considered an asset.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in critical-facilities engineering or mission-critical operations (electrical and mechanical infrastructure, commissioning, 24/7 operations) with multi-site scope, preferably within hyperscale, colocation, or large-scale industrial environments.
  • Demonstrated experience building and owning KPI tracking, audit frameworks, or operational governance processes across multiple sites.
  • Experience operating across the construction-to-operations boundary, including facility onboarding and commissioning handover, with accountability for the acceptance decision.
  • Demonstrated progression from hands-on site-level execution to leadership of operational governance or process improvement, including leading a team.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to lead through functional direction without direct line authority across site teams.
  • Sound technical judgment and the ability to hold technical accountability (approve standards and deviations) while aligning with enterprise standards.

Benefits

At IREN, we offer a comprehensive,market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect ourcommitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performanceand long-term growth.

Compensation

  • Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications.
  • Relocation and Living-out-allowance (as applicable and based on successful candidate circumstances)

Health & Wellness

  • 100% company paid health insurance premiums (medical, dental, and vision) for employees, 75% company paid coverage for dependents
  • Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Voluntary life, critical illness, and accident coverage available
  • Health Savings Accounts (HSA) – when combined with the High-Deductible Health Plan
  • Employee Assistance Program and wellness resources

Retirement& Financial Wealth

  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Paid professional development and access to financial planning and legal services

Time Off& Leave Programs

Growth& Development

  • Professional development to support certifications, continuing education, or role related training

Community& Culture

  • Company events and team-building activities

jobs.description:
Description

WHO WE ARE

Come join the company at the center of how the world adopts AI securely. Cyera’s mission is to give enterprises the confidence to embrace AI safely — deciding exactly what it can see and do as it reaches deeper into the business. We started by solving the hardest problem in data security: finding and securing data faster and more precisely than anyone thought possible. That foundation is now the essential AI trust infrastructure for the Fortune 1000. We’re hiring mission-driven talent to put those leaders at the center of our story.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring a Senior GRC Analyst- Risk to build and run Cyera's enterprise risk register. You will design the risk management framework, own the full risk lifecycle from identification to closure, and turn risk data into clear decisions for leadership. This is a builder role: you will set the foundation, then operate it at scale as Cyera grows.

You will report to the GRC Manager and work closely with Security, Engineering, IT, Legal, Privacy, Finance, and business leaders.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Build the framework

  • Design and document Cyera's enterprise risk management methodology, including risk taxonomy, scoring model (likelihood and impact), risk appetite and tolerance thresholds, and treatment options
  • Align the program to recognized frameworks such as ISO 27001, NIST CSF and NIST 800-30, SOC 2, and ISO 42001 for AI risk
  • Establish risk ownership, RACI, escalation paths, and governance cadence with the GRC Manager and leadership
  • Standardize risk register structure, naming conventions, and ID nomenclature so risks are consistent and audit-ready

Operate the risk register

  • Own the enterprise risk register end to end: identification, assessment, treatment, monitoring, acceptance, and closure
  • Run recurring risk assessments and workshops with control owners and business stakeholders
  • Track treatment plans, remediation due dates, and risk acceptances, and follow up with owners to keep work moving
  • Map risks to controls, policies, audit findings, vendor risks, and incidents so the register reflects the full picture
  • Maintain evidence and documentation that supports internal and external audits

Report and influence

  • Produce risk reporting and dashboards for the GRC Manager, CISO, and governance committees, including top risks, trends, and KRIs
  • Translate technical and operational risk into clear business language for executives
  • Prepare risk inputs for audits, customer security reviews, and board or leadership updates

Improve and scale

  • Automate intake, scoring, and reporting through GRC tooling and simple workflows (Jira, GRC platforms, spreadsheets) before adding complexity
  • Integrate risk management with TPRM, vulnerability management, incident response, AI governance, and change management
  • Train risk owners and build reusable templates, guides, and playbooks

Requirements

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3 to 5 years of experience in GRC, IT risk, information security risk, or enterprise risk management
  • Hands-on experience building or significantly maturing a risk register and risk assessment process, not just maintaining one
  • Working knowledge of at least two of ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NIST 800-30, NIST 800-53, or SOC 2
  • Strong grasp of risk scoring, risk appetite, treatment, and acceptance, and the judgment to apply them practically
  • Experience mapping risks to controls and supporting external audits
  • Ability to run risk conversations with engineers and executives, and to hold owners accountable without slowing the business
  • Clear, concise writing and reporting skills
  • Comfort working in a fast-moving SaaS or cloud environment with changing priorities
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience

Nice to have

  • Certifications such as CRISC, CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, or ISO 31000 Risk Manager
  • Experience with GRC platforms (for example Anecdotes, Drata, Vanta, ServiceNow IRM, or Archer) and Jira workflows
  • Exposure to AI risk management, ISO 42001, or the EU AI Act
  • Familiarity with multi-framework environments such as PCI DSS, FedRAMP, C5, or ENS
  • Experience at a security or data security vendor
  • Data Privacy and Protection experience

﻿

COMPENSATION INFORMATION:

Compensation Range: $100,000 - $120,000.

The range represents total compensation, and may include incentive for sales roles, equity or benefits, as applicable.

This compensation range represents Cyera’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of posting, and Cyera may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. We're also a Certified B Corp, and 25% of the company is owned by Phoresters. When the company grows, everyone has a stake in that.

About the Product team

Our ambition is to become the number one platform for premium hair, beauty and aesthetics businesses globally. For our Product & Engineering organisation, that means understanding the people behind those businesses and building thoughtful, reliable products that make a real difference to how they work.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for experienced Product Managers at both mid and senior level to help shape products that support hair, beauty and medspa professionals to run thriving businesses.

Working closely with Design, Engineering and Data, you’ll turn customer insights into meaningful product improvements, balancing strategy with hands-on delivery. You’ll take ownership of high-impact initiatives, shape clear roadmaps, prioritise what matters most and deliver measurable outcomes. Along the way, you’ll build strong relationships across teams and regions, bring clarity to complex challenges and help raise the bar for product quality. For more senior team members, there’s also the opportunity to mentor others and influence product direction beyond your own domain.

What You'll Do

  • Own a product area end-to-end, defining its strategy, long-term roadmap and key bets in line with Phorest’s mission and measurable outcomes.

  • Lead complex, high-impact initiatives across squads, functions or regions. Partner with Engineering, Design and Product Operations to align dependencies early, reduce ambiguity and deliver through influence rather than authority.

  • Lead discovery by talking with customers, analysing data, running experiments and validating assumptions. Build close partnerships with regional teams and join customer calls regularly to bring in-market insight into decisions.

  • Balance customer value, strategic fit and commercial return when prioritising; communicate trade-offs, risks and progress clearly to senior stakeholders and partners.

  • Collaborate across teams—including Commercial, Success, Support, Product Marketing and regional teams—to align readiness, bring feedback into solutions and support adoption.

  • Own outcomes beyond delivery: track adoption, customer outcomes and commercial measures such as ROI and ARR; use post-launch data and feedback to learn, improve and ensure initiatives reach their intended impact.

  • Keep your product area organised and transparent with a current roadmap, prioritised backlog, clear requirements, initiative metrics and proactive progress updates. Build strong business cases for major investments.

  • Mentor and support other Product Managers, sharing feedback and helping strengthen product practice across the team.

Who You Are

You’re an experienced product manager who combines strong product thinking with a practical, collaborative approach. You communicate clearly, make good judgement calls and keep the team aligned on what matters most.

You have:

  • Between 5-8 years’ Product Management experience, with a proven track record of successful product launches and significant business outcomes.

  • Strong customer empathy and a structured approach to problem solving; you seek insight directly from salons and end-users and validate assumptions continuously.

  • Strategic thinker who connects product and roadmap decisions to Phorest’s strategy, customer value and commercial outcomes, balancing user needs, business value and technical feasibility.

  • Confidence partnering with Engineering and Design to challenge ideas constructively and make trade-offs that deliver great outcomes.

  • A trusted leader by influence: you build credibility, align senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams without relying on authority, and communicate clearly and persuasively.

  • Organised and dependable, bringing clarity and consistency to complex workstreams and following through from discovery to impact.

  • Outcome-focused and analytical: you define success by impact, set and track KPIs (including ROI and ARR), analyse product usage and turn evidence into actionable insights.

  • A supportive mentor who coaches other Product Managers in product craft, discovery and prioritisation, helping strengthen team capability.

  • Resilient and adaptable: you navigate ambiguity with composure, stay focused on results and adjust when new evidence emerges.

  • Strong knowledge of Agile methodologies and product development frameworks; experience with tools such as Jira and Looker.

  • Experience in hair, beauty or wellness, consumer products, mobile products or a relevant product area is an advantage, as is experience selecting and managing suppliers or vendors.

Benefits

jobs.description:
Director, NeoCloud Sales (Sell-To)

Backblaze (Nasdaq: BLZE) | Reports to the Chief Revenue Officer | Remote, US-based

Salary range: $195,000 - $240,000 plus variable pay and RSUs. Target OTE $325,000 - $400,000 60:40 base to variable.

How We Got Here

We started by building storage servers from scratch in a Palo Alto apartment to save 90% on hardware. Turns out hard constraints make for pretty good engineering. That discipline forged a platform that performs as well or better than competitors, scales to multi-exabyte workloads, and costs a fraction of what AWS or Google charge. AI infrastructure runs on data. Storage gets hard at scale. We've been breaking, rebuilding, and improving that storage layer for 20 years.

Today, the world's leading AI infrastructure providers, neoclouds, and data-intensive businesses run on Backblaze. Our platform includes:

  • B2 Overdrive - high-throughput object storage engineered for AI infrastructure, GPU workloads, and massive-scale data pipelines
  • B2 Neo - white-label enterprise cloud storage powering neocloud platforms for AI, HPC, and media
  • B2 Cloud Storage - S3-compatible object storage with predictable pricing, free egress, and no lock-in
  • Computer Backup - automatic, continuous endpoint backup for Macs and PCs

500,000+ customers. 175 countries. Nasdaq: BLZE. backblaze.com

The Role

NeoClouds are GPU-rich, AI-native infrastructure providers, and they need fast, affordable, S3-compatible storage at scale. Backblaze is the high-performance capacity storage layer for AI. We have mapped the top 80 NeoClouds and Frontier Labs worldwide, about 70% in the US and 30% in EMEA, and we already have traction in the US, UK, and France.

You will build and run this segment as its own business inside the CRO organization: your own quota, your own team, and the mandate to decide how Backblaze wins each account. These deals look more like telecom or federal sales than SaaS. Cycles are long, buyers sit at the CXO level, and contracts run three to five years. Often Backblaze sits behind the NeoCloud's own storage service, so the work continues after signature, in SLAs, support, and integration.

This is not a territory to inherit. If your instinct is to wait for a playbook, or to hand the CXO calls to someone more senior, this isn't the right fit. If your instinct is to pick the first five accounts, write the pursuit plan, and take the call yourself, keep reading.

What You Will Own & Build

Own

  • Logos. Land and grow five of the Top 25 NeoClouds as meaningful customers, and land 25 more from the rest of the list.
  • TCV. Deliver $20M in total contract value across the base. We measure on TCV because these customers sign multi-year commitments.
  • Expansion. Grow the existing NeoCloud base outside committed contracts such as CoreWeave.
  • Pipeline and forecast. Own both for the whole segment, and carry a named-account number yourself.
  • Your team. Hire, onboard, and coach a growing team of BD Pursuit Specialists / AEs. Set the KPIs and ARR-conversion targets they are paid against.

Build

You build this with the Field CTO, Strategic Partnerships, an SE and Cloud Operations beside you, and with your AEs as they join.

  • Route to market. Own the Sell-To motion for the segment, with its own plays for each type of NeoCloud. No two NeoClouds behave alike, so you choose the play for each account. Write the pursuit plan for the Top 25 NeoClouds: the order we go after them, the buying group in each, and the play for each.
  • Sell-With. This is Strategic Partnerships' motion, and you work it in tandem with them, not underneath them, on OEM and ISV flywheels with partners such as NVIDIA, Super Micro, Weka, VAST, and AMD. When a NeoCloud wants help selling Backblaze storage to its own customers, you and Strategic Partnerships decide together how to staff it.
  • Deal structure. Negotiate SLAs, IP, revenue share, and infrastructure-as-a-service terms when Backblaze runs behind a NeoCloud's service.
  • Internal selling. Bring our Executives (including the CEO), Cloud Operations and Engineering into each integration, and keep them engaged after signature. This is as much internal selling as external.
  • Executive sponsorship. Secure a Backblaze executive sponsor and a customer executive sponsor for every priority account, then run CXO conversations without senior leadership in the room.
  • Transition. Take over open NeoCloud opportunities and existing coverage from the current BD owners by the end of Q1. Exceptions are handled case by case.

What We Are Looking For

  • Infrastructure fluency. You know or can get fluent in the NeoCloud infrastructure stack: GPU compute, networking, storage, and orchestration. You can spar with our Field CTO on architecture without needing drive-level detail. Storage experience is a plus.
  • Executive presence. You have built SVP, CTO, and CXO relationships and can run those meetings alone. You have landed and expanded multi-year committed contracts.
  • Product depth. You can work with senior product and development teams at a NeoCloud and hold a strategic conversation, not only a commercial one.
  • OEM and ISV deal experience. You have negotiated service integration, SLAs, IP, revenue share, and infrastructure-as-a-service structures. You have done these deals, not watched them.
  • Seller of record. You have carried a quota and closed deals with your name on them.
  • Leadership. You have led a small, senior, quota-carrying team and still carry a number yourself. A Specialist team in a large organization, esp in early days a plus.
  • Executive sponsorship. You win sponsors on both sides of the table.

A Plus (though not essential)

  • Experience selling to NeoClouds, GPU clouds, hyperscalers, cloud providers, or AI infrastructure companies
  • Experience building a new segment or coverage model from scratch
  • Familiarity with S3-compatible object storage, data egress economics, and AI/ML data pipelines

This Is Not the Role for You If

  • You want to run an established territory rather than build a new segment
  • You no longer carry a number yourself
  • You need senior leadership in the room to open or close CXO conversations
  • You see SLA, IP, and revenue-share terms as legal's problem, not yours
  • You treat partners and Cloud Operations as a handoff rather than as part of the deal

How We Will Interview

We will ask you to bring a plan on how you'd build the market for NeoCloud, and tell us what you would do differently. We will ask about how you worked on building executive relationships . We will ask for your own view of how you would approach this role. You will hold cross-functional conversations with the Field CTO/ VP of our SE Team and Strategic Partnerships, because you will work beside them every day. And you may go through a panel, so we can see how you work.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and equity package
  • Full benefits including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) with matching
  • RSU grants for full-time employees
  • ESPP program
  • Flexible vacation policy
  • Maternity & paternity leave
  • MacBook to use for work, plus a generous stipend to personalize your workstation
  • Childcare bonus (human children only)
  • Fertility treatment and support
  • Learning & development program
  • Commuter benefits
  • A collaborative and transparent culture that supports a healthy work-life balance

Pay Transparency and Equal Opportunity

To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.

Compensation for this role will be $195,000 - $240,000 plus variable pay and RSUs. Target OTE $325,000 - $400,000 60:40 base to variable.

We are committed to fostering a workforce where all employees feel a sense of belonging regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, socio-economic status, ability, veteran status, and education. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based.

What this opportunity involves

We’re looking for US-based, actively practicing physicians (MD/DO) to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation program. General and internal medicine are our main focus. While each project involves unique tasks, contributors may:

  • Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor “trap” answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
  • Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;

  • Work within three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You’re improving the AI tools you’ll eventually use yourself.

What we look for

This opportunity is a good fit for US-based physicians open to part-time, non-permanent projects. Ideally, contributors will have:

  • Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified with the issuing medical board);
  • Board certification or completed residency training, with recent direct patient care (attending-level preferred);
  • Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
  • Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
