jobs.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks an Active Directory / Identity Engineer to own and sustain the Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services environment supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Active Directory / Identity Engineer to own and sustain the Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services environment supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This senior engineering position manages AD objects, organizational units, Group Policy Objects, trusts, replication, schema governance, delegated permissions, domain services, and recovery capabilities.

The Active Directory / Identity Engineer ensures that directory services remain secure, available, recoverable, and aligned with USMEPCOM operational and cybersecurity requirements. The engineer supports domain and forest planning, account and group administration, site replication, trust relationships, Group Policy, domain-controller lifecycle activities, backup, restoration, and modernization.

The position also evaluates and tests approved Identity, Credential, and Access Management capabilities, including potential Okta integrations and other identity-modernization technologies. These modernization activities complement—not replace—the position’s requirement for direct, hands-on AD DS engineering expertise.

The engineer works closely with cybersecurity, Service Desk, systems, cloud, network, application, COOP, and Government identity stakeholders. This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Occasional after-hours maintenance, incident response, COOP exercises, on-site support, or travel may be required.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Active Directory / Identity Engineer will:

  • Serve as the senior technical owner for the USMEPCOM Active Directory Domain Services environment.
  • Install, configure, maintain, update, troubleshoot, and recover Active Directory services and supporting components.
  • Create, modify, disable, delete, and manage authorized AD objects in accordance with approved processes.
  • Manage organizational units, users, computers, groups, service accounts, shared resources, and other directory objects.
  • Maintain the domain plan, organizational-unit plan, site plan, trust plan, Group Policy design, and related architecture documentation.
  • Design and maintain an organizational-unit structure that supports administration, policy application, security boundaries, and delegated management.
  • Manage organizational-unit permissions and administrative delegation using least-privilege principles.
  • Review delegated access and correct excessive, obsolete, inherited, or conflicting permissions.
  • Develop, test, implement, maintain, and troubleshoot Group Policy Objects.
  • Manage GPO links, inheritance, precedence, security filtering, loopback processing, WMI filters, backups, version history, and recovery.
  • Evaluate proposed GPO changes for security, operational, and customer impact before production implementation.
  • Identify and resolve conflicting, obsolete, duplicative, or ineffective Group Policy settings.
  • Manage trust relationships with enterprise and external AD structures.
  • Configure, validate, monitor, and troubleshoot domain and forest trusts within approved security boundaries.
  • Review trust direction, transitivity, authentication scope, name-suffix routing, and related security settings.
  • Manage AD sites, subnets, site links, replication schedules, bridgehead behavior, and replication topology.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot replication latency, failures, lingering objects, directory inconsistencies, and site-topology problems.
  • Maintain the health of domain controllers, directory databases, SYSVOL, DFS Replication, time synchronization, and AD-integrated DNS dependencies.
  • Monitor Flexible Single Master Operations roles and support approved role transfer or seizure when necessary.
  • Plan and execute domain-controller installation, replacement, upgrade, demotion, and retirement activities.
  • Develop and implement approved plans to transition Active Directory to supported versions.
  • Manage AD schema governance and coordinate tightly controlled schema extensions.
  • Evaluate schema-change requests for compatibility, replication impact, operational risk, recovery requirements, and required approvals.
  • Maintain current directory schematics, architecture diagrams, object models, administrative boundaries, trust diagrams, and replication diagrams.
  • Administer account and group changes escalated from approved Service Desk and access-management processes.
  • Support troubleshooting of authentication, authorization, account, group-membership, policy, trust, replication, and directory-permission issues.
  • Coordinate with the Service Desk to improve identity-related ticket routing, troubleshooting, escalation, and knowledge content.
  • Provide advanced engineering support during identity, authentication, domain, and access-management incidents.
  • Identify widespread authentication failures or other outage signals and escalate them through approved incident-response procedures.
  • Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action development for recurring directory and identity incidents.
  • Develop and maintain Active Directory backup, restoration, and forest-recovery procedures.
  • Test system-state backups, directory restoration, authoritative and non-authoritative recovery, deleted-object recovery, and forest-recovery procedures.
  • Support COOP exercises, disaster-recovery testing, recovery validation, and actual continuity events.
  • Document recovery results, deficiencies, corrective actions, and lessons learned.
  • Evaluate and test approved ICAM and identity-modernization technologies.
  • Support integration testing between Active Directory and Okta or other Government-approved identity platforms.
  • Validate identity synchronization, account linking, authentication flows, group or attribute mappings, provisioning behavior, access controls, and failure handling.
  • Support testing of approved federation and modern authentication protocols such as SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth, SCIM, LDAP, or comparable technologies.
  • Coordinate identity-integration activities with cybersecurity, application owners, cloud teams, network teams, and Government identity authorities.
  • Develop test plans, test cases, expected results, rollback procedures, and validation evidence for identity integrations.
  • Evaluate modernization options while preserving required AD DS authentication, authorization, Group Policy, trust, recovery, and administrative capabilities.
  • Assess modernization proposals for interoperability, security, operational support, lifecycle, resiliency, and mission impact.
  • Automate approved directory administration, health validation, reporting, audit, and configuration activities where appropriate.
  • Review directory audit information and report activity outside approved baselines.
  • Support enforcement of DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides and approved security baselines.
  • Monitor and remediate applicable directory-service vulnerabilities, configuration findings, and policy deficiencies.
  • Support Risk Management Framework controls, assessment evidence, Plan of Action and Milestones activities, and authorization documentation.
  • Follow approved incident, problem, change, configuration, access, release, security, and quality-management processes.
  • Maintain standard operating procedures, recovery plans, configuration baselines, change records, test results, and technical documentation.
  • Provide directory-service health, availability, capacity, risk, issue, modernization, and recovery information for program reporting.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience where permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • Minimum of eight years of relevant experience in Active Directory engineering, identity engineering, Windows infrastructure, systems engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Direct, hands-on experience engineering and administering Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services in an enterprise environment.
  • Experience managing AD objects, organizational units, Group Policy Objects, trusts, replication, schemas, delegated permissions, and directory recovery.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex authentication, authorization, Group Policy, replication, trust, and directory-services issues.
  • Experience planning or supporting Active Directory backup, restoration, disaster recovery, or forest recovery.
  • Experience testing identity integrations or evaluating enterprise identity-modernization technologies.
  • Understanding of the distinction between core AD DS administration and external ICAM, federation, or cloud-identity services.
  • Knowledge of enterprise identity security, least privilege, delegated administration, account management, and access-control principles.
  • Ability to develop and maintain architecture diagrams, domain plans, OU plans, Group Policy documentation, trust diagrams, recovery procedures, and technical standards.
  • Ability to support after-hours maintenance, COOP exercises, disaster-recovery testing, and critical incident response when required.
  • Strong written, verbal, analytical, and technical problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • Experience integrating Active Directory with Okta.
  • Experience with Microsoft Entra ID or hybrid identity.
  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense ICAM initiatives.
  • Experience with SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth, SCIM, LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, and federation technologies.
  • Experience with Active Directory Federation Services or comparable identity-provider technologies.
  • Experience with PowerShell scripting and directory-administration automation.
  • Microsoft identity, Windows Server, Azure, or security certification.
  • Okta Certified Administrator, Okta Certified Consultant, or comparable Okta certification.
  • CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or another relevant security certification.
  • Experience with CAC, PIV, certificate-based authentication, public key infrastructure, or DoD enterprise authentication.
  • Experience applying DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides to Active Directory and Windows infrastructure.
  • Experience supporting DoD Risk Management Framework controls and authorization activities.
  • Experience designing or testing identity capabilities aligned with Zero Trust principles.
  • Experience with Active Directory monitoring, privileged-access management, identity governance, or audit tools.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification.

Skills and Competencies

  • Enterprise Active Directory engineering and administration.
  • Organizational-unit and Group Policy design.
  • Trust, replication, schema, and permissions management.
  • Directory backup, restoration, and forest recovery.
  • Identity integration and modernization testing.
  • Authentication and authorization troubleshooting.
  • Security baseline and least-privilege implementation.
  • PowerShell and directory-administration automation.
  • COOP and disaster-recovery support.
  • Architecture and technical-documentation development.
  • Cross-functional identity and infrastructure coordination.
  • Strong configuration discipline and attention to detail.
  • Ability to retain deep AD DS expertise while evaluating modern ICAM capabilities.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.

jobs.title: RevOps Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About demandDrive:demandDrive is a growth-focused go-to-market agency that helps B2B organizations accelerate pipeline and revenue through integrated sales, marketing, and revenue operations solutions.
jobs.description:
About demandDrive:

demandDrive is a growth-focused go-to-market agency that helps B2B organizations accelerate pipeline and revenue through integrated sales, marketing, and revenue operations solutions. We partner with companies ranging from emerging businesses to enterprise brands to design and execute customized programs that align strategy, technology, and execution across the full customer journey. Our services include sales development, demand generation, digital marketing, website development, CRM optimization, and GTM systems support - all built to deliver measurable business outcomes. At our core, we combine smart technology, data-driven processes, and talented people to help clients grow faster and operate more efficiently.

Position Overview - RevOps Engineer:

As our RevOps Engineer, you'll own client CRM engagements end to end, from the first discovery call through blueprint, build, documentation, launch, enablement, and post-launch ROI reporting. You'll be assigned your own clients and own those relationships directly.

The split is roughly 85% client work, 15% internal. That 15% means supporting demandDrive's own HubSpot instance: executing builds and requests from our sales and marketing teams, keeping our data clean and documented, and helping use our portal as the proving ground for things we later bring to clients.

Who We're Looking For:

You know the feeling when you open a client's portal for the first time and find 340 unused properties, four lifecycle stages that all mean "kind of interested," and a pipeline where half the deals closed in 2023 and nobody noticed? Most people see a mess. You see a system that hasn't been designed yet.

We want a builder first. Someone who thinks in object models and data flows, not just workflows, and who would rather script a change from the command line than click through it one property at a time. You already work in Claude Code. You've connected it to a CRM through an MCP server, used the HubSpot CLI to build and deploy, and you have opinions about when to automate a build versus do it by hand. When something new ships, whether it's a HubSpot release, a new MCP server, or a new model, you've already tried it, watched it do something dumb, and rebuilt it with the right guardrails.

You're also business minded. Clients will hand you a list of twenty requests. You can tell which three are business critical and will actually move the needle, translate the goal behind them into clear, actionable next steps, and explain why the rest can wait.

We're an agency, so you won't be building in the background while an account manager talks to the client. You'll be in the room. You'll run discovery, write the blueprint, build it, and train the team on it. Some engagements are greenfield. Some are rescues. Some are Salesforce migrations for a team that's terrified of the change. No two CRMs look the same, and that's the fun part.

Job Responsibilities:

Client delivery (~85%)

  • Lead discovery and working sessions with stakeholders across sales, marketing, sales engineering, and post-sale delivery to document current-state process, data sources, and gaps, and translate client goals into clear, actionable next steps.
  • Separate business-critical requests from nice-to-haves, and prioritize the work that will actually move pipeline and revenue for the client.
  • Write the build blueprint covering object model, lifecycle stages, pipeline design, property architecture, automation logic, and reporting plan, then walk clients through it to sign off before configuration starts.
  • Architect and build the full CRM foundation, most often in HubSpot: property architecture, record and object customization, create forms, lifecycle and status frameworks, the Lead object, routing and assignment logic, and multi-pipeline deal processes across sales and post-sale motions.
  • Build CLI-first: use Claude Code, the HubSpot CLI, and MCP servers to script configuration, migrations, and integrations so builds are faster, version-controlled, and repeatable across clients.
  • Run data consolidation, deduplication, standardization, and migration projects, and stand up the enrichment and data quality automation that keeps the database clean after launch.
  • Design attribution models and build the dashboards and reporting infrastructure leadership actually uses to forecast, treating reporting as a design input from day one rather than a final step.
  • Build with AI where it earns its place: Claude Code and MCP-connected agents working against live CRM data, plus HubSpot's Breeze agents, Agent Builder, and Breeze Assistant, with the governance and guardrails to match.
  • Deliver enablement including recorded training, written documentation, admin enablement for the client's internal system owner, and post-launch support through the first weeks of real usage.
  • Build and maintain documentation of each client’s HubSpot instance, covering object model, properties, automation logic, and integrations, so the system stays understandable long after launch.
  • Track and report on post-launch ROI, tying what was built back to the business goals set in discovery.
  • Scope change orders and retainer expansions honestly, and tell clients when they should wait on something rather than buy it.

Internal HubSpot support (~15%)

  • Provide support for demandDrive's HubSpot instance by executing internal builds and projects that align with the defined strategy.
  • Execute requests from internal teams, from quick fixes to real builds.
  • Keep our own data, reporting, and automation in the shape we'd want a client's to be in.
  • Build and maintain documentation of our instance so configuration, automation, and changes are tracked.
  • Pilot new HubSpot releases, MCP servers, and AI tooling internally so we know what's real before we recommend it.

Job Requirements & Qualifications:

  • CRM Experience (HubSpot Is Non-Negotiable) You need deep, hands-on HubSpot expertise across Sales Hub and Marketing Hub at minimum, ideally Service and Content too. Custom objects and association labels. Lifecycle stage architecture. The Lead object and lead pipelines. Multi-pipeline deal processes with stage gating and required properties. Workflow automation at real complexity. Permissions, teams, and portal governance. Custom report builder and dashboards. You know where the platform's edges are and you design inside them instead of promising around them. Hands-on Attio or Salesforce experience is a plus.
  • Builder Mindset: Claude Code, CLIs & MCPs You build with Claude Code day to day, not just as a chat window. You've used CLIs, including the HubSpot CLI, to build and deploy, and you've set up or built MCP servers that connect Claude to a CRM. You reach for the command line when it's faster and more repeatable than clicking, you keep your work in version control, and you review what an agent produced before it touches a client's live data.
  • Data Hub, Enrichment & Data Quality Working knowledge of HubSpot Data Hub: data sync, data quality automation, formatting rules, property validation, datasets, and where credits get consumed. You understand HubSpot's native enrichment across automatic, continuous, and manual modes, what it can and can't fill in, and how to set realistic expectations on match rates. You've run a real deduplication and cleanup project and know when native tooling is enough versus when a third-party tool needs to come in.
  • AI-First Thinking, Including Agent Builder You approach every problem by asking where AI does the heavy lifting. You're familiar with HubSpot's Agent Hub and Agent Builder, building custom agents and agentic workflows on live CRM data, wiring triggers, configuring knowledge sources, and testing before publishing. You think about credit consumption, run limits, and human review on consequential actions, because agents that write to the CRM without guardrails create cleanup work instead of removing it. You're also comfortable building with Claude and other leading models outside of HubSpot, and you stay current as the landscape moves.
  • Client Leadership & Business Judgment You can run a discovery session with a VP of Sales and a skeptical sales engineer in the same room, ask the questions that surface the real process, scope a solution, and communicate clearly about what you're building and when it lands. You can say "that's out of scope, here's what it would take" without it becoming a problem. You translate client goals into clear, actionable next steps, and you can tell which requests are business critical and will actually move the needle versus which ones just feel urgent. You don't need hand-holding in client situations.
  • Reporting & Attribution You've built forecasting, closed-won, and operational accountability reporting that leadership trusts. You understand attribution models, first touch versus latest touch and why most clients don't need multi-touch, and how to enforce data capture so the reports hold up.
  • Technical Foundation Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, and the command line. You can build an integration or debug a sync issue without pulling in a developer. Light scripting in Python or JavaScript is a plus, as are custom coded actions in HubSpot workflows.
  • Data Migration You've moved real data into HubSpot from spreadsheets, another CRM, or somewhere worse. You know how to build import templates, handle associations, backfill historical records, and set expectations about what won't survive the trip.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience at a HubSpot Solutions Partner or RevOps consulting firm.
  • HubSpot certifications, especially Architecture, Data Integrations, or Solutions Partner-level credentials.
  • Attio or Salesforce experience, particularly migrations to or from HubSpot.
  • Experience building your own MCP servers, Claude Code skills, or HubSpot developer projects.
  • Automation tools like Zapier, n8n, or Make for connecting systems HubSpot doesn't natively reach.
  • Familiarity with compliance-adjacent constraints like SOC 2, CMMC, and HIPAA, and how they shape what belongs in a CRM.
  • Active in HubSpot or RevOps communities.

Compensation & Benefits:

  • Salary: $80,000 to $90,000, depending on experience.
  • Schedule: M-F, 9am-5pm - hybrid or remote work model (must reside in the U.S.).
  • Structure: Full-time, reporting to the Sr. RevOps Manager.
  • Health coverage and other health & wellness benefits via BCBS, vision care, dental coverage (Delta Dental), paid paternity & maternity leave, life & disability insurance, 401(k) matching.
  • Paid time-off and 14 paid holidays.
  • Positive team culture.
  • Company laptop, full tech stack, tools, and other resources provided by demandDrive.

jobs.title: Director of HR
jobs.excerpt: WHO ARE WE? Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company.
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

Base salary: $170,000 to $190,000. Plus an annual bonus paid as a flat amount rather than a percentage of base.

Launch Potato is about 200 people, profitable, and growing. The performance management system that got us here was built by our SVP of Talent, and he still runs it. That system becomes yours.

You're inheriting something that works. There's a levels framework, a rating scale, a calibration process, and managers who have been through several cycles. It got us to 200 people. Your job is deciding what carries forward and change-managing the rest, across an org that moves fast and adopts new processes.

We want someone who'll find the version that works and then hold it there while the company gets good at it.

If you want to own a function, make it extraordinary, and be judged on whether it actually got better, keep reading.

Why This Seat

  • Real ownership, immediately. Performance, total rewards, and compliance are yours to own rather than support. You'll defend a compensation number in front of a CFO who checks it.
  • An SVP who wants to hand this over. Not one who says that and then rewrites your deck. The explicit goal is that the HR function runs without him.
  • Executive reach by default. Calibration and leveling decisions live with the C-suite, and you present your own work. You won't spend year one convincing anyone that performance management matters.
  • Leverage is part of the mandate, not a side project. We are tech-first and AI-forward, which means we can run lean teams and do more with less. You'll push that further, build the tooling managers actually open, and make everything easier without taking substance out of it. Nobody will ask you to do it the slow way.

How This Team Is Led

From Kris Osborne, SVP of Talent.

I'll tell you what I want and what the constraints are and then get out of the way. I don't rewrite people's work. If I disagree with where you landed you'll hear it from me early, and if you still think you're right then push back, because I'd rather change my mind than have you go quiet and build something you don't believe in.

I ask before I decide. When something changes the shape of this team the people on it hear it from me first and they get a real say in it, not a heads up after it's done.

I care about the outcome and I'm not going to do your job for you. Bring me a problem and I'll work it with you, but I'm not going to take it off your plate and hand it back finished.

I'm hiring this seat because I want someone we can all learn from. Bring me a better answer than mine and I'll take it.

What You'll Bring

All required.

  • A full performance cycle you owned end to end, not supported. Owned more than once, at 150 people or more. Design, timeline, manager prep, calibration, rollout, retro.
  • Compensation and benefits you've owned. Band design, benchmarking methodology, benefits renewals, the annual comp cycle. You can defend a number to a CFO.
  • HR compliance as standing scope, not as a project. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. You've inherited a backlog and cleared it.
  • A people system that outlasted you. Built, adopted, and still recognizable two cycles later.
  • Leverage you built that people adopted. You've automated or rebuilt part of a people process so it ran faster, the quality held or improved, and the team actually used it. Adoption is the test here, the same way durability is the test above.
  • Experience taking a company our size to materially larger, on headcount or revenue, more than once. You know what breaks first at the next stage because you've watched it break.
  • Empowered your team to raise the bar. You have clear examples of coaching, mentoring, and growing a team that created extraordinary outcomes.

This is a player-coach seat. Managers here lead a team and deliver work personally, at every level.

Nice to Have

  • You have opinions about what performance management gets wrong, and specific examples of what you changed
  • You can tell a process problem from a manager-capability problem, and you fix the right one
  • You're the person who says the uncomfortable thing in a calibration room

What You'll Own

Performance management. The mid-year and annual cycles end to end: design, timeline, communication, execution. What the cycle needs to produce and what to cut. A timeline published early enough that managers plan around it. The retro after each one, and the judgment about when a change is warranted and when to leave it alone.

Total rewards. Band design and the benchmarking methodology behind it. Benefits renewals and the economics underneath them. The annual comp cycle, with leveling and pay kept connected.

Compliance. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. The current backlog, plus the escalation and coverage protocols that follow it.

Manager enablement. Preparing managers for real performance conversations, including the one where someone rated themselves higher than their manager did. The calibration process, including where two managers apply the same bar differently. Playbooks and self-service resources so a manager gets an answer without booking a meeting. Standing support for the roughly three dozen front-line managers who get it reactively today.

Leverage and tooling. Finding the parts of everything above that shouldn't be done by hand, and fixing them. Building what a manager will actually open rather than what looks good in a demo. Taking time out of the cycle while the conversations get better rather than thinner.

The team. An HR Business Partner and a Total Rewards and People Analytics lead. Both are strong at what they do and both have room to grow. You set their decision rights: where they decide, where they recommend, where it comes to you.

What Great Looks Like

In your first year:

  • The annual cycle ships on your timeline and you own it
  • Managers are calibrated before the cycle rather than corrected after it
  • Every person leaving a check-in has one clear thing to work on, and the conversation that produced it was a real one
  • The compliance backlog is closed and stays closed
  • The cycle costs managers less time than the year before, and the conversations are better rather than thinner
  • Your two reports hold more decision authority than they did at the start

This Isn't the Right Seat If

  • This would be your first Director-level people role
  • You lead with policy and risk. Compliance is required here and it isn't the center of the work
  • You want to redesign the cycle every year
  • You see tooling and automation as somebody else's job
  • You're looking for a recruiting role. Recruiting sits elsewhere in the function

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

jobs.description:
Sr. Enterprise Account Executive — Build the Future of Food & Beverage Operations

B2B / Saas - Remote based, USA (Midwest preferred)

Why This Role Matters

At SafetyChain, we’re transforming how the world’s leading food and beverage manufacturers run their plants — making them safer, smarter, and more efficient. This isn’t a “feature-and-demo” role — it’s a business transformation sale. As an Enterprise Account Executive, you’ll be at the forefront of that movement, helping iconic brands like Tyson, Chobani, Butterball, Whole Foods, Cargill, and Driscoll’s move from clipboards and spreadsheets to real-time digital operations.

Who We Are

SafetyChain is a rapidly scaling SaaS platform built for manufacturers who never stop improving. We help food and beverage operations digitize quality, safety, and production processes — unlocking real-time visibility and performance insights across the plant floor.

Our impressive client base includes renowned brands like Albertsons, Clif Bar, Tyson Foods, and Whole Foods. Join a dynamic, collaborative team driven by innovation, agility, and rapid growth.

Our products solve for:

  • Quality and Safety Management: Helping companies ensure product safety and quality by providing tools to manage compliance with regulatory standards (e.g., FDA, USDA).
  • Supplier Management: Assisting with the management of supplier documentation, performance, and risk to ensure adherence to quality and safety standards.
  • Compliance Management: Offering tools to ensure companies meet industry regulations and standards, reducing the risk of non-compliance and associated penalties.
  • Production and Operational Efficiency: Helping companies optimize production processes by improving visibility, traceability, and real-time monitoring.

What You’ll Do

Your mission: Reporting to the VP of Sales, win new logos, build business cases that prove ROI, and help enterprise manufacturers modernize their operations.

You will:

  • Drive new revenue by leading complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles (6–12 months) from first conversation to close.
  • Engage executives and plant leaders — from Quality to Operations to the C-Suite — and align SafetyChain’s solutions to their business imperatives.
  • Run world-class discovery to uncover operational pain, build value, and quantify impact.
  • Deliver business case presentations that connect digital transformation to measurable ROI.
  • Negotiate and close multi-year agreements that drive mutual success.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales Engineers, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success to ensure every win becomes a long-term partnership.

What Success Looks Like

  • You meet or exceed a $1M+ ARR quota, putting up numbers quarter after quarter.
  • Your deals are built on impact, not discounts.
  • You become a trusted advisor inside your accounts, not just another vendor.
  • You bring insight and rigor to every conversation — from your first call to the boardroom.
  • You share ideas, wins, and laughs — because sales is serious business, but it should still be fun.

What You’ll Bring

  • 5–10 years of enterprise SaaS sales experience, consistently overachieving $1M+ quotas.
  • Proven success in solution or consultative selling — uncovering business challenges and building tailored solutions.
  • Comfort engaging at multiple levels — plant floor to C-suite.
  • Familiarity with selling into manufacturing, food, beverage, or compliance-driven environments.
  • Strong business acumen, presentation, and negotiation skills.
  • A disciplined, process-driven approach using modern CRM and sales methodologies (MEDDICC, Challenger, Force Management, or equivalent).

Nice to Have

  • Experience with OEE, SPC, ISO/SQF, or compliance systems.
  • Background in food & beverage or manufacturing technology.
  • Track record of influencing digital transformation initiatives.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • People who care — smart, humble, collaborative teammates who make work fun.
  • People. A humble, hungry, helpful team that has your back.
  • Growth. Real opportunity to shape how we scale — plus stock options and professional development investment.
  • Balance. Remote flexibility, self-care PTO, and a culture that values outcomes over hours.
  • Momentum. A fast-growing SaaS company with a product customers love and a market full of whitespace.

Our Values

Quality Above All. Build the best experiences for our teams and our customers.

Innovate for Impact. Design solutions that make manufacturing better for everyone.

Work Smart. Operate with precision, discipline, and purpose.

Grow Together. One team, with help and hustle.

This isn’t just about hitting quota — it’s about helping companies produce the food that feeds the world, safely and efficiently. If you thrive on meaningful work, complex problem solving, and collaborating with ambitious teams, you’ll fit right in.

Job Type: Full-time

Equal Opportunity Employer: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law applicable to the state in which you work.

Speed, precision, and growth are your playground. As a Junior Video Editor, you are the engine room of our post-production team. You’ll support Senior Editors by assembling footage, handling high-volume versioning, and applying the finishing touches that make our ads pop.

    • Execute fast-paced edits for social media (TikTok, Reels, Shorts), focusing on pacing, music syncing, and basic transitions.

  2. Handle Versioning & Resizing

    • Take approved "hero" edits and adapt them for various platforms and aspect ratios (9:16, 4:5, 16:9) ensuring no visual quality is lost.

    • Create multiple variations of ads (changing hooks, swapping music, updating CTAs) to support our aggressive A/B testing strategy.

  3. Manage Assets & Organization

    • Maintain a pristine digital workspace. ensuring all project files, assets, and exports are named and organized according to High Scale’s strict workflows.

  4. Learn & Level Up

    • Absorb feedback from Art Directors and Senior Editors to refine your technical skills and storytelling ability.

    • Stay current with social media trends to understand what editing styles are trending on TikTok and Instagram.

Who You Are

  1. A Rising Talent

    • 1–3 years of experience in video editing (freelance or agency). You have a portfolio that shows potential, rhythm, and a good eye for composition.

  2. Technically Proficient

    • You know Adobe Premiere Pro inside and out. You are comfortable with keyboard shortcuts and efficient workflows.

  3. Fast & Detail-Oriented

    • You can work quickly without sacrificing quality. You double-check your export settings and catch small mistakes before anyone else does.

    • You are organized and follow instructions precisely.

  4. Eager to Learn

    • You check your ego at the door. You view feedback as an opportunity to get better, not a criticism.

    • You want to build a career in performance marketing and commercial editing.

  5. Excellent Communicator

    • Strong English proficiency is required. You can communicate clearly with a global remote team via Slack and Zoom.

Perks & Benefits

  • Growth Opportunities: We promote from within. Master this role, and the path to Video Editor and Senior Editor is open to you.

Country Manager South Africa

As Country Manager South Africa, you understand the crucial role strong business ecosystems play in driving economic growth, social inclusion, and sustainable development. You bring a solid local network of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and partners, combined with proven experience in programme management and team leadership. Do you thrive on building meaningful partnerships, leading a result-driven team, and creating lasting impact across your country? This is your opportunity!

About PUM

PUM is a unique organisation committed to making a positive impact on a global scale. With a network of 1,200 skilled voluntary experts, we collaborate with ambitious entrepreneurs in 26 countries and 12 programmes, sharing expertise to strengthen business ecosystems and create economic, social, and environmental value. We work closely with SMEs, as well as the organisations that support them. We believe in the power of collaboration and in the magic that happens when diverse perspectives come together; Together we grow!

The role

You will lead the country acquisition team in South Africa, consisting of 6Country Representatives on a freelance basis who engage change-driven SMEs to participate in PUM's impactful programmes. You hold end-to-end responsibility for client relationship management after acquisition, ensuring continuity, quality of engagement, and strategic alignment. You will be part of the Africa regional team, reporting to the head of region and collaborating closely with 15 other country managers in the region, 12 programme managers, as well as other departments such as recruitment and communications & partnerships. Your daily activities will be varied and challenging:

  • You develop and implement the Country Impact Plan (CIP) in line with PUM’s mission, strategy, and organisational ambitions.

  • You center on strengthening business ecosystems, based on strategic analysis and in line with PUM’s programmes. You are able to establish partnerships and collaborate with wider networks of entrepreneurs, business organisations and other enabling organisations to advance business ecosystems.

  • You identify, develop, and secure funding opportunities from institutional donors, foundations, corporate partners, and other possible sponsors, contributing to the sustainability and growth of PUM's impact in South Africa.

  • You foster strategic partnerships with SMEs and stakeholders through proactive account management and ongoing engagement, building trust and long-term impact, while expanding PUM's visibility, credibility and country influence.

  • You build, lead, and coach the country representative team, safeguarding the quality and continuity of acquisition.

  • You ensure team capacity, motivation, accountability, and performance through effective people management, including organising country team meetings (CTMs).

  • You qualify new clients using assessment criteria that emphasise diversity, inclusion, and alignment with PUM’s green and social goals within business ecosystems.

  • You approve project proposals, ensuring accurate and complete information so programme managers can identify the right expert match.

  • You collaborate closely with programme managers to ensure alignment, shared goals, and successful projects. Occasionally, you will welcome and accompany visiting experts.

  • You personally engage with clients after acquisition, ensuring continuity, quality of engagement, and strategic fit.

  • You lead professional briefing and debriefing sessions to ensure quality assurance, data collection, and learning.

  • You monitor performance and use data to share insights and improve results. 

  • You ensure compliance with organisational policies, quality standards, and project timelines.

Who are you?

As Country Manager, you combine strategic vision with operational excellence. You understand the challenges that local SMEs face and know how to translate entrepreneurial ambition into tangible impact. Does this sound like you?

  • You are a proactive, hands-on and strategic thinker with a bachelor's or master's degree.

  • You bring at least 10 years of experience in a coordinating role and leading a commercial or acquisition-focused team.

  • You bring in strong fundraising capabilities through a thorough understanding of local donor opportunities.

  • You have a strong local SME network and a deep understanding of business ecosystem development in your country.

  • You are familiar with European work culture and experienced in remote collaboration within international organisations.

  • You demonstrate strong intercultural communication skills and collaborate effectively across departments and stakeholders.

  • You have proven leadership and accountability skills, with experience in performance management and stakeholder engagement.

  • You are experienced in managing a remote team operating across the country.

  • You are willing to travel occasionally within South Africa for project development visits, partnership meetings, and country team meetings.

  • You are strongly focused on impact, quality, and measurable results.

  • You thrive in an organisation in growth and transition and enjoy contributing to further professionalisation.

  • You are data-driven and comfortable using digital tools, including Microsoft 365.

  • You have excellent command of English.

  • You are permanently based in South Africa, preferably Johannesburg or Cape Town, and available for 37.5 hours per week.

What we offer

This assignment is offered on an independent contractor basis with an expected commitment of approximately 37.5 hours per week, up to a maximum of 1.800 hours per year. The initial assignment is for one year, with the possibility of extension based on organisational needs and a successful collaboration. You will receive a competitive fee aligned with local market standards, reflecting the responsibilities and scope of the role. As an independent contractor, you are responsible for your own taxes, social security contributions, insurance and any other statutory obligations that apply in your country of residence. Reference checks and a declaration of good conduct are part of the selection process. At PUM, we celebrate diversity and inclusion as essential pillars of our organisation. We embrace the uniqueness of each individual, fostering an environment where everyone can thrive by being their authentic selves.

Ready to make a difference? Join us!

Becoming a Country Manager at PUM isn’t just a career move; it’s a chance to drive meaningful change. Working at a volunteer organisation like PUM offers extra fulfilment. In addition to the benefits mentioned, here’s what else awaits you:

  • Building a brighter future: Contribute to the sustainable development of communities, cultivating a profound sense of fulfilment

  • Optimal knowledge utilisation: Put your expertise to its best use, making tangible impact on businesses worldwide.

  • Continuous learning: Embrace new perspectives and gain insights by connecting with diverse people and cultures.

  • Building a professional network: Collaborate with a vast network of stakeholders, including institutional funders, government entities, and NGOs.

  • International exposure: Immerse yourself in a multicultural environment, broadening your horizons.

Apply now and be part of something truly meaningful!

Get inspired by one of our successful projects within our Social & Educational programme in South Africa: The revitalisation of Dimbaza Industrial Park in South Africa - PUM

In the case of a high volume of applications we reserve the right toclose the vacancy early and begin interviews before the deadline on 17 November 2026. Please submit your CV and motivation letter in English.

Highlights

Picture yourself as people manager, leading the country team of South Africa. Are you ready to shape a brighter tomorrow? Join PUM and let’s make a lasting impact together!

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Our client is a software company that helps property managers inspect properties and turn what they find into clear, shareable reports. They've been at it for over ten years, profitable and self-funded the whole way, and today tens of thousands of people use it, together capturing over 100 million inspection photos. They're now putting real energy into paid social, and this role builds the creative behind it.

Your Role

Paid social is a new channel for a product like this, and the hard part is easy to say and tricky to do: explain an operational tool without making ads that feel technical or corporate. You own the fun, social-first concepts, from the first spark of an idea to the finished creative. You learn how customers actually work, find the human tension inside their problems, and turn it into something people want to watch. This is not a make-briefs-and-wait role: you carry an idea from spark to finished ad and care how it lands. You do not need to master every craft; you define the outcome, keep the idea intact, and judge the work that reaches the audience.

You'll

  • Come up with social-first ad concepts and hooks that earn attention in the first few seconds
  • Turn a dry, operational insight into something relatable, funny, or genuinely fun to watch
  • Make the work: writing, filming on a phone, editing, or directing a freelancer or AI tool, whatever the idea needs
  • Write clear briefs so a creator, editor, or tool can run with an idea without losing it
  • Test variations and let what the audience responds to shape what you make next
  • Keep every finished ad accurate, clear, and relevant to the people who might buy

You Bring

  • A real feel for short-form video and social content, shown through anything you've made: side projects, a personal account, school, freelance, or a job
  • An instinct for hooks: you get why a video keeps someone watching past the first seconds
  • Clear writing, enough to brief an idea so someone else executes it faithfully
  • Comfort being hands-on where it helps, without needing to be an expert at every part
  • You actively use AI tools in your creative work, and can say how
  • Good spoken and written English, since the team is US-based and fully remote

Years are not the point here; instinct and taste are.

Bonus Points

  • Creative for B2B or SaaS, or any product people think is unglamorous
  • A sense for paid-social performance: hook rate, retention, testing
  • Any brush with property management, real estate, or field services

What's Offered

  • Fully remote, anywhere in LATAM with a few hours of overlap with US Pacific time
  • Part-time or full-time, whatever fits; the work matters more than the hours
  • What we'd estimate for a role like this: around $1,500 to $2,500 USD/month for full-time (roughly $9 to $14 per hour), paid weekly in USD as a contractor. Part-time is welcome and paid hourly. Share the range that fits your level and we'll go from there
  • Up to 20 days paid time off a year (prorated for part-time)
  • Real creative ownership: your ideas ship and reach audiences in weeks, not quarters

This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts , Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Washinton DC, Maryland, Delaware. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.

  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

  • Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue
  • All candidates must be located in one of the following states: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts , Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Washinton DC, Maryland, Delaware

Annual OTE Salary
$152,000—$190,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

jobs.description:
FICO (NYSE: FICO)is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!

The Opportunity


FICO builds the analytics and decisioning technology behind some of the highest-stakes decisions in the world economy including the FICO Score, the standard measure of consumer credit risk in the US, and FICO Platform, an API-first applied intelligence platform delivering real-time decisions across fraud detection, credit risk, regulatory compliance, marketing, and customer engagement. This is mission-critical, low-latency, heavily regulated software where auditability and controlled change are non-negotiable. This role sits at the point where that technology is being built and operated in an agentic-first way. As coding agents take on an increasing share of the software lifecycle, the engineer's role shifts from hand-writing code to directing, specifying, and verifying the output of a fleet of specialised agents, working through a structured harness of guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that transforms raw model capability into production grade engineering. The successful candidate will bring the engineering judgement that agents cannot replicate: the ability to define what good looks like, encode it with sufficient precision for agents to achieve it, and recognise when they have not, applying that judgement to architecture, correctness, trade-off analysis, and the design of the work itself.


What You’ll Contribute

  • Collaborate with Product teams to translate early stage ideation into structured Proof of Concepts, establishing clear technical feasibility and scope.
  • Produce detailed specifications and acceptance criteria that enable coding agents to generate correct, maintainable, and well-architected output, taking full ownership of the resulting code through to deployment.
  • Apply rigorous quality standards to all agent generated output, ensuring it meets the same level of scrutiny as hand written code within a regulated decisioning context.
  • Operate effectively within the agentic harness, utilising established guides, including AGENTS.md files, architectural rules, and reference documentation alongside automated sensors such as linters, fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers.
  • Identify the root cause of recurring agent errors and work with the harness team to implement systemic controls, ensuring the same class of failure cannot recur across the codebase.
  • Maintain the accuracy and currency of repository documentation, specifications, and contextual knowledge, treating these as a shared system of record for both human engineers and agents.
  • Apply focused technical judgement to architecture decisions, edge case analysis, latency and integration risk, auditability requirements, and any determination that falls outside the appropriate scope of agent autonomy.

What We’re Seeking

  • Demonstrable experience in software engineering within large, complex codebases, with a strong foundation in software architecture, testing practices, and long-term maintainability.
  • Practical experience working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor with a clear understanding of their capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use within a production engineering workflow.
  • The technical judgement to critically evaluate agent generated output, identify subtle errors or architectural weaknesses, and make informed decisions about when to intervene in the agent workflow.
  • The ability to communicate technical requirements with precision, producing specifications and definitions of done that are unambiguous, testable, and actionable by both agents and engineering colleagues.
  • A disciplined approach to verification, instinctively questioning correctness, building appropriate checks and test coverage, and applying particular rigour in regulated and mission-critical delivery contexts.
  • A results-oriented approach to delivery, with accountability for the quality and correctness of shipped work rather than volume of code produced.
  • Familiarity with relevant technologies including Python, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, AWS or Azure, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, ML model deployment, or real-time decisioning systems.
  • Experience with spec-driven development, context engineering, or agent orchestration in a team environment is a significant advantage, as is knowledge of regulated or audited software delivery processes and controlled change management.
  • A background in decisioning, credit risk, fraud detection, analytics, optimisation, or data engineering would be advantageous; candidates who can also articulate a considered approach to human-AI collaboration including delegation boundaries, human oversight, and earning autonomy through demonstrated quality will be of particular interest.

Our Offer to You

  • An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers and Earn the Respect of Others.
  • The opportunity to make an impact and develop professionally by leveraging your unique strengths and participating in valuable learning experiences.
  • Highly competitive compensation, benefits and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so.
  • An engaging, people-first work environment offering work/life balance, employee resource groups, and social events to promote interaction and camaraderie.

Sales Support Specialist

Full-Time | M–F 8:30–5:30 Central | 100% Remote (U.S.)

  • $36,000 base + commission
  • Full base from day one — including every day of training
  • 100% inbound — no cold calling, no prospecting, no list building

About Us

At EIDLexit we help small business owners resolve their SBA disaster loan (EIDL) debt. Most are frightened, embarrassed, and out of options when they reach out. We believe every person is made in the image of God and deserves honest guidance in the hardest financial season of their life.

We are a Christian-led company looking for people who want to build a career here — not pass through. You can read what we believe at eidlexit.com/about-us.

We're scaling fast, with lead volume growing every month.

Sales Support Specialist

Our closers sit across from small business owners on the hardest financial day of their year. Your job is to make sure every one of those conversations starts prepared, on time, and with trust already built.

This is a dedicated sales-support career role. You do not sell or close. You make our closers faster.

What You Will Do

  • Respond to new leads fast and earn the consult with tactical empathy.
  • Book, confirm, and recover consults so closer calendars stay full of qualified conversations.
  • Route every borrower to the right calendar.
  • Gather documents and complete the HubSpot record so closers never open a blank file.
  • Keep borrowers moving after the consult with clear, honest next steps.
  • Hand every objection, legal question, or SBA question to the closer. You do not answer them.

What You Will Never Do

  • Sell, close, or quote fees or terms.
  • Give legal advice or predict SBA forgiveness decisions.
  • Make promises on behalf of the SBA or an attorney partner.

How You Will Be Measured

Show rate, file completeness, speed to lead, closer capacity, and call quality. No dial-count quotas.

The Opportunity

Every lead is inbound. These are business owners actively searching for help with a serious financial problem — they raised their hand and asked us to call. Answer rates are high because they need us.

You are the first person a client speaks with. We train in tactical empathy, not scripts and pressure. Those skills transfer anywhere.

What You Need

Every item below is checked in your application:

  • Hands-on HubSpot CRM experience. You have logged calls and notes and kept contact and deal records current.
  • Experience working with AI. You have used an AI tool such as ChatGPT, Copilot, or Claude in your work.
  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. as a W-2 employee.
  • Availability Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM–5:30 PM Central, and full-time through the three-week onboarding and training block.
  • A reliable computer with a webcam, stable high-speed internet, and a private, quiet place to take calls.

What We're Looking For

  • A warm, clear communicator who leads with empathy and listens before they talk.
  • A problem solver. When two numbers don't match, you check before you act.
  • Detail-oriented. You read every instruction and follow structured processes consistently.
  • You genuinely care about the person on the other end of the call, and you would rather tell someone the truth than close them. We hire people of every background who want to work this way.
  • Coachable and self-motivated in a remote environment.
  • Prior appointment-setting, lead-response, or customer-support experience is a plus but not required. No degree required.

This is not for you if you close by pressure or you're not comfortable with people in financial distress.

What We Offer

  • Four weeks of paid time off a year. One full week is yours the day you start — not prorated, no waiting period, no matter when in the year you join. The other three weeks accrue across the calendar year, prorated from your start date. PTO covers vacation and sick time.
  • All national holidays paid, plus Good Friday and Christmas Eve
  • Health insurance and retirement launching Q1 2027
  • KPIs you know in advance and see every month. Annual pay reviews run off those same measures, so nothing lands as a surprise
  • Ongoing paid communication, tactical empathy, and career training
  • The full commission structure in writing — every tier, every percentage — during the interview process and again before you accept an offer. You will know exactly how you get paid before you decide

Position Details

Full-time W-2, 100% remote, open to candidates across the United States. You must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. as a W-2 employee — we do not sponsor visas. A few states may be unavailable depending on where we are registered to employ; we will tell you early if yours is one of them.

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM Central Time. That's 6:30 AM–3:30 PM Pacific and 9:30 AM–6:30 PM Eastern.

You'll be on video all day through Microsoft Teams. You need a reliable computer with a webcam, stable internet, and a quiet workspace.

How to Apply

The application comes first: a few short-written questions, about ten minutes. Then five stages, and we'll tell you where you stand at each one.

  1. A short video interview: scripted questions you record on your own time, about six minutes. Nothing to schedule.
  2. Skills assessments: about thirty-five minutes.
  3. A live interview with sales management.
  4. A set of workstyle and aptitude assessments: about two hours, and you can split it across sittings. We only send these to our finalists.
  5. A final conversation with leadership.

Job searching is stressful enough. We don't ghost candidates. You'll hear back either way.

EIDLexit is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Sales Development Representative

Argano | Remote

About Argano

Argano is the first and largest Global Specialist Consultancy exclusively focused on the design and delivery of High-Performance Business Operations with our AI-forward approach to transformation. We pioneer intelligent and connected solutions for our clients' operational environments across customer engagement and service, revenue management, finance and planning, supply chain, and workforce optimization, driving both efficiency and the agility to innovate product, service, and organizational design at the speed of today's market. Competitive advantage, cost optimization, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth are our North Stars and our promise to our clients.

About the Role

The Sales Development Representative (SDR) is a critical, high-visibility role at the tip of the spear of Argano's revenue engine. This is not a passive lead-routing position - it demands a driven, intellectually curious professional who thrives on the hunt, builds genuine business relationships, and is energized by connecting complex enterprise challenges to transformative solutions that extend our clients' commercial agility, profitability, customer experience, and growth.

You will own the top of the sales funnel - identifying, engaging, and qualifying prospective clients within an assigned Argano business unit (BU). You will partner with senior sales professionals, Practice Leaders, Presales, Alliances, and Marketing to build a consistent, high-quality pipeline. This role carries a quota with meaningful incentive compensation, and high performers have a clear path to senior sales roles within Argano.

What You'll Contribute

  • Bring positive energy, curiosity, a competitive spirit, and a relentless ambition for success to every prospect interaction and team engagement.
  • Drive brand awareness by educating the market and sharing thought leadership with executive-level prospects, while aligning Argano's solutions to meaningful business outcomes.
  • Identify and pursue high-value opportunities - net new and expansion - by targeting ideal customer profiles and connecting their business challenges to Argano's capabilities.
  • Execute high-volume, high-quality outbound prospecting via phone, email, and LinkedIn to engage C-suite, VP, and Director-level decision-makers at enterprise companies.
  • Lead structured discovery conversations that go beyond surface-level qualification to uncover real business challenges, desired outcomes, and decision-making dynamics.
  • Align closely with your internal partners on target account priorities, messaging strategy, and lead pursuit to ensure a coordinated and effective approach to the market.
  • Utilize the full RevTech stack to increase connect rates, deliver timely and relevant messaging, and continuously improve outreach effectiveness.
  • Maintain accurate records of prospect data, activity, and market insights in Outreach and Salesforce to support campaign optimization and pipeline integrity.
  • Participate in ongoing training to deepen knowledge of buyer personas, Argano's service offerings, and the technology solutions we deliver.
  • Consistently meet and aim to exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual pipeline generation goals.

What We're Seeking

  • 3-5 years of experience in Sales Development, Business Development, or Inside Sales in a technology-driven environment - ideally selling enterprise software or technology consulting services to large, complex organizations.
  • A Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Information Technology, or a related field - or equivalent professional experience.
  • Proficiency with tools including Outreach, Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Microsoft Office, ZoomInfo, and a dialer such as Orum or Nooks.
  • Experience with territory prioritization, ICP definition, and targeted outreach strategy - not scripted calling.
  • The ability to tailor messaging to specific verticals, pain points, and buying triggers, with the judgment to know which accounts warrant pursuit and when to push versus pull back.
  • Professional maturity, business insight, and strong communication discipline in a high-expectation, self-managed environment.
  • A critical thinker and competitor who uses data to improve performance and wants to be great at this - not just good enough.

What Great Looks Like in This Role

The best SDRs at Argano are students of the craft. They invest in understanding their prospects' businesses before picking up the phone, write outreach that earns a reply, and run discovery conversations that uncover real pain and genuine urgency. They hand off opportunities that the sales team is excited to work - and they treat every rejection as information, not defeat. If you are hungry to learn and ready to compete at a high level, this role will reward you.

Why Argano

  • A market-leading consulting practice with deep client relationships and a strong reputation for delivery excellence - making your outreach credible from the first call.
  • Competitive base salary, uncapped incentive compensation, and a full benefits package.
  • A collaborative, high-performance culture where SDRs are respected contributors to revenue - not an afterthought.
  • A clear path to more senior sales roles for high performers who demonstrate results and ambition.

We’re looking for a highly organized, relationship-driven Social Affiliate & Influencer Marketing Specialist to help grow and activate our creator, ambassador, and affiliate network.

This role will focus on the day-to-day execution required to turn creator partnerships into a scalable acquisition and revenue channel — identifying the right creators, managing outreach and onboarding, supporting product seeding and campaigns, driving consistent content creation, and optimizing affiliate performance.

  • Experience with consumer brands; experience in wellness, beauty, food/beverage, or other regulated categories is a plus
  • An entrepreneurial, test-and-learn approach and comfort operating in a fast-moving environment

Benefits

PERKS & BENEFITS
